IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p141/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p141/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p141/r2.claim: He expands ألا يسجدوا as ألا يا هؤلاء اسجدوا, supplying the vocative address.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p141/r2.anchor: أراد: ألا يا هؤلاء اسجدوا لله

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p141/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p141/r3.speaker: الشاعر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p141/r3.claim: An unnamed poet’s address to Salma’s house supplies a poetic example alongside the expanded vocative construction.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p141/r3.anchor:
وقال الشاعر :
يا دار سلمى يا اسلمي ثم اسلمي

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p187/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p187/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p187/r4.claim: He expands ألا يسجدوا لله as ألا يا هؤلاء اسجدوا لله, supplying an addressed group and imperative.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p479/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p479/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p479/r3.claim: Islahi holds that these two verses are God's insertion, not part of the lapwing's speech, linking the discourse to Arabia at the Qur'an's revelation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p479/r3.anchor: By adding these words, the discourse

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p479/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p479/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p479/r4.claim: The insertion says Satan diverted them from the God who reveals hidden things in heaven and earth, knows what is concealed and revealed, and owns the glorious throne.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p479/r4.anchor: what people conceal and what they reveal

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p479/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p479/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p479/r5.claim: Because “knows what you conceal and what you reveal” is unsuitable for a lapwing to say, Islahi takes these words as God's own speech.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p479/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p479/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p479/r6.claim: The word al-khabʾ refers to what is hidden and revealed by God in heaven and earth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p479/r6.anchor: all the hidden things of the heavens and the earth

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p479/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p479/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p479/r7.claim: The hidden things of heaven include the sun, moon, rain, plants, Venus, and Mercury; those of earth include vegetation, trees, seas, and springs, all created and governed by God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p479/r7.anchor: the sun, the moon, the rain

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p205/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p205/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p205/r9.claim: Al-khabʾ is a hidden thing, from khabaʾa, “to conceal”; the passive object is named with the verbal noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p205/r9.anchor: الخبء: الشيء المخبوء، من خبأت الشيء خبأ: سترته، وسمي المفعول بالمصدر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r4.claim: Al-khabʾ is a verbal noun used for something hidden, including rain, plants, and other unseen things God conceals.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r4.anchor: والخبء: مصدر أطلق على المخبوء، وهو المطر والنبات وغيرهما مما خبأه تعالى من غيوبه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r5.claim: The majority read الخبء with a still bāʾ and hamza; Ubay and Isa transfer the hamza's vowel to bāʾ and omit the hamza.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: الخبء، بسكون الباء والهمزة. وقرأ أبي، وعيسى: بنقل حركة الهمزة إلى الباء وحذف الهمزة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r6.speaker: عكرمة، عبد الله، مالك بن دينار
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r6.claim: Ikrima, Abd Allah, and Malik ibn Dinar are associated with a form using alif instead of hamza, explained by applying pausal pronunciation in connected speech or by a dialectal hamza change.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r6.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة: بألف بدل الهمزة، فلزم فتح ما قبلها، وهي قراءة عبد الله، ومالك بن دينار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r7.claim: The competing explanations for alif in place of hamza are balanced: a weak dialectal form versus the rare transfer of pausal pronunciation into connected speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r7.anchor: قيل: وهي لغة ضعيفة، وإجراء الوصل مجرى الوقف أيضا نادر قليل، فيعادل التخريجان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r8.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r8.claim: Sibawayh records transfer of the hamza's vowel to bāʾ with deletion of hamza among some speakers of Tamim and Asad.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r8.anchor: ونقل الحركة إلى الباء، وحذف الهمزة، حكاه سيبويه، عن قوم من بني تميم وبني أسد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r9.speaker: أبو حاتم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r9.claim: Abu Hatim rejects the alif reading as ungrammatical, arguing that deleting hamza would yield الخب and changing it would yield الخبي.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r9.anchor: وقراءة الخبا بالألف، طعن فيها أبو حاتم وقال: لا يجوز في العربية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r10.speaker: المبرد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r10.claim: Al-Mubarrad says Abu Hatim ranked below his peers in grammar, though he was the most learned person in his hometown.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r10.anchor: قال المبرد: كان أبو حاتم دون أصحابه في النحو، ولم يلحق بهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r11.claim: The apparent syntax attaches في السماوات to الخبء, meaning the hidden things in the heavens.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r11.anchor: والظاهر أن في السماوات متعلق بالخبء، أي المخبوء في السموات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r12.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r12.claim: Al-Farra says في and من can alternate in Arabic; on that analysis, في السماوات attaches to يخرج and means “from those in the heavens.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p230/r12.anchor: وقال الفراء في ومن يتعاقبان بقول العرب: لأستخرجن العلم فيكم، يريد منكم

DURR-FULL:v6p352/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses the hidden thing brought forth as the unseen.
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {يخرج الخبء} قال: الغيب

DURR-FULL:v6p352/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r2.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r2.claim: Ikrima interprets the hidden thing as a secret.
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله {يخرج الخبء} قال: السر

DURR-FULL:v6p352/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r3.claim: Qatada gives the same interpretation as Ikrima: the hidden thing is a secret.

DURR-FULL:v6p352/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r4.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r4.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib identifies the hidden thing as water.
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب في قوله {يخرج الخبء} قال: الماء

DURR-FULL:v6p352/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r5.speaker: حكيم بن جابر
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r5.claim: Hakim ibn Jabir identifies the hidden thing as rain.
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r5.anchor: عن حكيم بن جابر في قوله {يخرج الخبء} قال: المطر

DURR-FULL:v6p352/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says the hidden things of heaven and earth include provision sent as rain and plants grown from the earth.
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r6.anchor: عن ابن زيد في الآية قال: خبء السموات والأرض ما جعل من الأرزاق والقطر من السماء والنبات من الأرض

FARRA:v2p291/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p291/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p291/r1.claim: Al-khabʾ is the hidden or unseen thing in the heavens and earth.
FARRA:v2p291/r1.anchor: وهو الغيب غيب السموات وغيب الأرض

FARRA:v2p291/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p291/r2.speaker: يقال
FARRA:v2p291/r2.claim: Another gloss identifies the hidden thing as rainwater from heaven and plants from earth.
FARRA:v2p291/r2.anchor: هو الماء الذي ينزل من السماء والنبت من الأرض

FARRA:v2p291/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p291/r3.speaker: عبد الله
FARRA:v2p291/r3.claim: Abdullah’s reading has min, from, where the common wording has fī, in; Farrāʾ says either preposition can be dropped in the idiom without changing the sense.
FARRA:v2p291/r3.anchor: في قراءة عبد الله (يخرج الخبء من السموات)

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd and Ibn Isḥāq take the phrase about prostrating to be the Hudhud’s speech.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r3.anchor: وهو قول ابن زيد وابن إسحاق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r4.claim: He objects that the Hudhud is not a law-bearing addressee, so it is unlikely to speak in a legal sense.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r4.anchor: ويعترض بأنه غير مخاطب، فكيف يتكلم في معنى شرع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r5.claim: After reflection, he regards the phrase as God’s parenthetical speech between the two reported utterances.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r5.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون من قول الله تعالى اعتراضا بين الكلامين وهو الثابت مع التأمل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r6.claim: The doubled form of “allā” supports the Hudhud attribution, while the light form rules it out and favors divine speech.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r6.anchor: وقراءة التشديد في «ألا» تعطي أن الكلام للهدهد، وقراءة التخفيف تمنعه وتقوي الآخر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r7.speaker: جمهور القراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r7.claim: The majority read “an lā yasjudū”; “an” may be an accusative apposition to their deeds or genitive apposition to the path.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r7.anchor: وقرأ جمهور القراء «ألا يسجدوا» ف «أن» في موضع نصب على البدل من أعمالهم وفي موضع خفض على البدل من السبيل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r8.speaker: جمهور القراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r8.claim: On the purposive reading, “an” attaches to “adorned” or “turned them away,” with the lām introducing a purpose object.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r8.anchor: أو يكون التقدير لأن لا يسجدوا ف «أن» متعلقة إما ب «زين» وإما ب «صدهم» ، واللام الداخلة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r9.speaker: ابن عباس، أبو جعفر، الزهري، أبو عبد الرحمن، الحسن، الكسائي، حميد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r9.claim: These authorities read “alā” as an opening particle; al-Kisāʾī pauses on yāʾ and then begins “usjudū.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وأبو جعفر والزهري وأبو عبد الرحمن والحسن والكسائي وحميد: «ألا» على جهة الاستفتاح ووقف الكسائي من هذه الفرقة على يا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r10.claim: That reading supplies an omitted vocative: “people” if God speaks, or “my people” or “rational ones” if the Hudhud speaks.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r10.anchor: وهذه القراءة مقدر فيها النداء والمنادى محذوف تقديره إن جعلناه اعتراضا يا هؤلاء ويجيء موضع سجدة، وإن جعلناه من كلام الهدهد يا قوم أو يا عقلاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r11.speaker: الكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r11.claim: Al-Kisāʾī supports the reading by a report from the Prophet that this location is a prostration place.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256/r11.anchor: واحتج الكسائي لقراءته هذه بأنه روي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه موضع سجدة

STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r5.claim: The account of Solomon's miraculous host and encounter with the Queen of Sheba ends with her embracing faith in the One God.
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r5.anchor: Solomon with his miraculous host of men, jinn, and birds and his encounter with the Queen of Sheba, who eventually comes before Solomon

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r1.speaker: الكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r1.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads the first word lightly: it is an attention particle, followed by yāʾ as attention or address, then the imperative; the written form joins the particles because their alif and hamza are not pronounced, so both readings coincide in sound and script but differ in analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r1.anchor: فقد عرفت أن قراءة الكسائي قوية لكثرة دورها في لغتهم

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r2.claim: Al-Samīn prefers yāʾ as an attention particle over an elided vocative to avoid excessive deletion; although alā precedes it, paired particles are defensible for emphasis, as Arabic usage attests.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r2.anchor: سمع بعضهم يقول: ألا يا ارحموني، ألا يا تصدقوا علينا

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r3.claim: Several poems by unnamed poets use alā yā before imperatives such as اسلمي, اسقياني, and اسمع; prose likewise has alā yā arḥamūnī and alā yā taṣaddaqū.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r3.anchor: سمع بعضهم يقول: ألا يا ارحموني، ألا يا تصدقوا علينا

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r4.claim: A further line has yā before a command without preceding alā; in a line about God's curse, yā may be vocative with an omitted addressee, though attention is preferred.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r4.anchor: يا دار هند يا اسلمي ثم اسلمي

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r5.claim: Al-Kisāʾī allows a full stop at yahtadūn, or test stops at alā yā, alā alone, or yā alone; the latter are not chosen stops because the particles need what follows to complete their sense.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r5.anchor: واعلم أن الكسائي الوقف عنده على " يهتدون " تام

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r6.claim: For the other readers, one parse expands allā to an lā: an governs the subjunctive, lā is extra, and the phrase is the object of yahtadūn after an omitted preposition, meaning toward not prostrating; al-Samīn cites the parallel liallâ yaʿlama.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r6.anchor: أصلها: أن لا، ف " أن " ناصبة للفعل بعدها

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r7.claim: A second parse makes the phrase an appositive to aʿmālahum, with a parenthetical interruption: Satan beautified their failure to prostrate to God.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r7.anchor: الثاني: أنه بدل من " أعمالهم " وما بينهما اعتراض

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r8.claim: A third parse makes it an appositive to al-sabīl, with an extra lā, meaning Satan turned them away from prostrating to God.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r8.anchor: الثالث: أنه بدل من " السبيل " على زيادة " لا "

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r9.claim: A fourth analysis treats the phrase as a purpose accusative attached either to zayyana or ṣaddahum; lā may be ordinary negation or extra.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r9.anchor: الرابع: أن { ألا يسجدوا } مفعول له

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r10.claim: With lā non-extra, Satan beautified or diverted them so they would not prostrate; if extra, it means he did so expecting or fearing their prostration.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r10.anchor: وفي " لا " حينئذ وجهان، أحدهما: أنه ليست مزيدة

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r11.claim: Al-Samīn prefers treating lā in the purpose-accusative parse as non-extra.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#2/r11.anchor: لأجل خوفه من سجودهم. وعدم الزيادة أظهر

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r1.claim: The fifth parse makes the clause predicate of an omitted subject referring either to أعمالهم, with لا negative, or to السبيل, with لا extra.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r1.anchor: الخامس: أنه خبر مبتدأ مضمر. وهذا المبتدأ: إما أن يقدر ضميرا عائدا على

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r2.claim: On the four earlier parses, a pause after يهتدون is invalid because what follows is governed by or substitutes for preceding wording; the omitted-subject parse allows it.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r2.anchor: وعلى الأوجه الأربعة المتقدمة لا يجوز الوقف على " يهتدون " لأن ما بعده: إما معمول له

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r3.speaker: القراء
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r3.claim: Since ألا is written joined, reciters do not pause between أن and لا in a test pause, but pause on the whole ألا.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r3.anchor: وقد كتبت " ألا " موصولة غير مفصولة، فلم تكتب " أن " منفصلة من " لا "

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r4.speaker: النحويون
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r4.claim: Grammarians pause on each word separately for clarification; connected spelling does not prevent that explanatory pause.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r4.anchor: والنحويون متى سئلوا عن مثل ذلك وقفوا لأجل البيان على كل كلمة على حدتها لضرورة البيان،

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r5.claim: Calling the writing joined is loose usage: the written form would retain nūn in أنلا, but assimilation merges its sound with لا.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r5.anchor: لأن حقيقة هذا أن يثبتوا صورة نون ويصلونها ب " لا " ، فيكتبونها: أنلا، ولكن لما أدغمت

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r6.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj requires prostration on al-Kisa'i's reading, which has an imperative, but not on the other readings, which lack one.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r6.anchor: وقد رتب أبو إسحاق على القراءتين حكما: وهو وجوب سجود التلاوة وعدمه؛ فأوجبه مع قراءة الكسائي

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says prostration is required on both readings: one commands it and the other censures those who omit it.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r7.anchor: هي واجبة فيهما، وإحدى القراءتين أمر بالسجود، والأخرى ذم للتارك

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj follows the apparent command, but the Sunnah indicates that prostration is recommended rather than obligatory.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r8.anchor: وهذا لو خلينا والآية لكان السجود واجبا، ولكن دلت السنة على استحبابه دون وجوبه،

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r9.claim: The command's force depends on whether God speaks or the hoopoe is quoted: divine command implies obligation absent contrary evidence, while the hoopoe's authority as proof is uncertain; the hoopoe is the apparent speaker.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#3/r9.anchor: على أنا نقول: هذا مبني على نظر آخر: وهو أن هذا الأمر من كلام الله تعالى، أو من كلام الهدهد محكيا عنه.

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r1.speaker: الأعمش
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r1.claim: Al-A'mash reads هلا, replacing hamza with هاء; لا may be geminated or light, as in Abdullah's codex.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r1.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش " هلا " ، و " هلا " بقلب الهمزة هاء مع تشديد " لا " وتخفيفها وكذا هي في مصحف عبد الله.

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r2.speaker: عبد الله
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r2.claim: Abdullah reads تسجدون with second-person address and an indicative nūn; another reading has ياء.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r2.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله " تسجدون " بتاء الخطاب ونون الرفع. وقرىء كذلك بالياء من تحت.

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r3.claim: With the indicative nūn, ألا is an exhortation whether geminated or light; light ألا may also be an offer or invitation.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r3.anchor: فمن أثبت نون الرفع فألا بالتشديد أو التخفيف للتحضيض، وقد تكون المخففة للعرض أيضا نحو:

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r4.speaker: عبد الله
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r4.claim: Abdullah's codex also has the addressed wording ألا هل تسجدون.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r4.anchor: وفي حرف عبد الله أيضا: " ألا هل تسجدون " بالخطاب.

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r5.claim: الذي may be genitive as adjective, apposition, or explanatory substitute; accusative as praise; or nominative as predicate of an omitted subject.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r5.anchor: قوله: { الذي يخرج الخبء } يجوز أن يكون مجرور المحل نعتا له أو بدلا منه أو بيانا،

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r6.claim: الخبء is originally the verbal noun of خبأت, to conceal, then denotes the concealed thing itself.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r6.anchor: والخبء مصدر خبأت الشيء أخبؤه خبئا أي: سترته، ثم أطلق على الشيء المخبوء.

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r7.speaker: التفسير
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r7.claim: Exegetical interpretation identifies the hidden thing in the heavens as rain and on earth as vegetation.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r7.anchor: وفي التفسير: الخبء في السماوات: المطر، وفي الأرض: النبات.

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r8.claim: The related word الخابية also omits hamza by convention, like البرية and الذرية according to some speakers.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r8.anchor: والخابية من هذا، إلا أنهم التزموا فيها ترك الهمزة كالبرية والذرية عند بعضهم.

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r9.speaker: أبي وعيسى
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r9.claim: Ubayy and Isa read الخب, moving the hamza vowel to باء and deleting hamza, comparable to رأيت الأب.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبي وعيسى " الخب " بنقل حركة الهمزة إلى الباء، وحذف الهمزة، فيصير نحو: رأيت الأب.

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r10.speaker: عبد الله وعكرمة ومالك بن دينار
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r10.claim: They read الخبا with explicit alif, explained as hamza replaced by a vowel-matched letter and the pause form carried into connected speech.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r10.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله وعكرمة ومالك بن دينار " الخبا " بألف صريحة. ووجهها: أنه أبدل الهمزة ألفا

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r11.claim: The author instead explains الخبا by retaining hamza after shifting its vowel to the preceding consonant, an established Arabic form like المرأة and الكمأة.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r11.anchor: وعندي أنه لما نقل حركة الهمزة إلى الساكن قبلها لم يحذفها، بل تركها فسكنت بعد فتحة فديرت

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r12.speaker: أبو حاتم
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r12.claim: Abu Hatim rejects الخبا as non-Arabic: deleting hamza after transfer should yield الخب, while substitution should yield الخبي; al-Mubarrad says Abu Hatim lagged behind his peers in grammar.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#4/r12.anchor: وقد طعن أبو حاتم على هذه القراءة وقال: " لا يجوز في العربية؛ لأنه إن حذف الهمزة ألقى حركتها على الباء،

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#5/r1.claim: في السماوات can modify الخبء, meaning hidden in the heavens, or يخرج, with في meaning من, as al-Farra' argues.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#5/r1.anchor: أنه متعلق ب " الخبء " أي: المخبوء في السماوات. والثاني: أنه متعلق ب " يخرج "

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#5/r2.speaker: الكسائي وحفص
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#5/r2.claim: Al-Kisa'i and Hafs read both verbs with second-person تاء; other readers use third-person ياء.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#5/r2.anchor: قوله: { ما تخفون } قرأ الكسائي وحفص بالتاء من فوق فيهما، والباقون بالياء من تحت.

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#5/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#5/r3.claim: Second-person suits the preceding command; third-person suits earlier absent pronouns, while Hafs may shift to the present audience or use iltifat.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#5/r3.anchor: فالخطاب ظاهر على قراءة الكسائي؛ لأن قبله أمرهم بالسجود وخطابهم به. والغيبة على قراءة الباقين

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#5/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#5/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya takes third-person as indicating hoopoe speech, and second-person as God's address to Muhammad's community.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#5/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " القراءة بياء الغيبة تعطي أن الآية من كلام الهدهد، وبتاء الخطاب تعطي أنها من خطاب الله

SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#5/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#5/r5.claim: The apparent reading is that the passage is the hoopoe's speech throughout.
SAMIN-DURR:27:24-25#5/r5.anchor: وقد تقدم أن الظاهر أنه من كلام الهدهد مطلقا

ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r2.claim: With tashdīd, Satan's beautification led them to abandon prostration; أن is accusative after فصدهم or genitive with an understood lām. With light hamza and lām, ألا introduces “prostrate”; only the light form has a prostration mark.
ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r2.anchor: فمن قرأ بالتشديد، فالمعنى وزين لهم الشيطان أعمالهم فصدهم ألا يسجدوا، أي فصدهم لئلا يسجدوا لله.

ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r3.claim: With the light form, ألا begins and alerts the hearer; pause at ألا يا, then begin the command اسجدوا لله.
ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r3.anchor: ومن قرأ بالتخفيف ف ألا لابتداء الكلام والتنبيه، والوقوف عليه ألا يا - ثم يستأنف فيقول: اسجدوا لله،

ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r4.claim: The light-reading form is a place of prostration, while the tashdīd reading is not.
ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r4.anchor: ومن قرأ بالتخفيف فهو موضع سجدة من القرآن ومن قرأ آلا يسجدوا - بالتشديد - فليس بموضع سجدة

ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r5.speaker: ذو الرمة
ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r5.claim: Dhū al-Rummah's ألا يا أسلمي illustrates the light ألا followed by ya outside a direct address.
ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r5.anchor: قول ذي الرمة. ألا يا أسلمي يا دار مي على البلى. . .

ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r6.speaker: الأخطل
ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r6.claim: Al-Akhṭal's ألا يا اسلمي likewise witnesses the light ألا يا construction.
ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r6.anchor: وقال الأخطل: ألا يا اسلمي يا هند هند بني بدر. . . تحية من صلى فؤادك بالجمر

ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r7.speaker: العجاج
ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r7.claim: Al-ʿAjjāj also uses the light ألا يا sequence in his address to Salmā.
ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r7.anchor: وقال العجاج يا دار سلمى يا اسلمي ثم اسلمي بسمسم أو عن يمين سمسم

ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r8.claim: He cites several witnesses because ordinary speakers rarely use يا except in direct address.
ZAJJAJ:v4p115/r8.anchor: وإنما فعلوا ذلك لقلة اعتياد العامة لدخول " يا " إلا في النداء

ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r1.claim: Anything kept hidden is called خبء.

ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r2.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r2.claim: The tafsir identifies the hidden things here as rain from heaven and plants from the earth.
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r2.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أن الخبء ههنا القطر من السماء، والنبات من الأرض.

ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r3.claim: The stronger interpretation is anything unseen, so the verse says God knows the unseen in heaven and earth; the following clause supports this.
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r3.anchor: ويجوز وهو الوجه أن يكون الخبء كل ما غاب، فيكون المعنى يعلم الغيب في السماوات والأرض.

ASAD-NOTES:27:20#n19/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:27:20#n19/r1.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:27:20#n19/r1.claim: Razi reads the parable as showing that even a lowly creature may know something Solomon, despite his wisdom, does not.

ASAD-NOTES:27:20#n19/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:27:20#n19/r2.speaker: Zamakhshari
ASAD-NOTES:27:20#n19/r2.claim: Zamakhshari sees a warning against self-conceit, a danger especially acute for learned people.
ASAD-NOTES:27:20#n19/r2.anchor: to which learned men, more than anyone else, are exposed (Zamakhshari)

ASAD-NOTES:27:20#n19/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:27:20#n19/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:27:20#n19/r3.claim: For background on the kingdom of Sheba, Asad refers to note 23 on 34:15.
ASAD-NOTES:27:20#n19/r3.anchor: As regards the kingdom of Sheba, see note 23 on 34:15.

ASAD-NOTES:27:23#n20/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:27:23#n20/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:27:23#n20/r1.claim: Satan here means people's immoral impulses, which persuaded them to evade accountability to a transcendent God and worship perceptible natural phenomena.
ASAD-NOTES:27:23#n20/r1.anchor: their own immoral impulses (which is the meaning of ash-shaytan in this context) had persuaded them that they should not submit to the idea of man's responsibility

ASAD-NOTES:27:23#n21/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:27:23#n21/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:27:23#n21/r1.claim: The hidden and manifest phenomena allude to the appearing and disappearing sun and other celestial bodies worshipped by Sabaeans and other ancient Semites.
ASAD-NOTES:27:23#n21/r1.anchor: An allusion to the appearance and disappearance of the sun and other celestial bodies which the Sabaeans - in common with almost all the Semites of antiquity - used to worship.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p383/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p383/r1.speaker: الكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p383/r1.claim: All readers except al-Kisai geminate the lām in allā yasjudū; al-Kisai lightens it, treats it without أن, pauses after alā-yā, then begins asjudū.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p383/r1.anchor: كلهم شدد اللام من قوله سبحانه: ألا يسجدوا [النمل/ 25] غير الكسائي فإنه خففها

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p383/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p383/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p383/r2.claim: With gemination, the phrase means Satan turned them aside so that they would not prostrate, or that he adorned their deeds so they would not prostrate; the purpose lām keeps the story's sequence intact.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p383/r2.anchor: من شدد ألا يسجدوا فتقديرها: فصدهم عن السبيل لئلا يسجدوا

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p383/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p383/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p383/r3.claim: The geminated form can also be heard as an appeal, ألا يا قوم أو يا مسلمون اسجدوا, contrasting the unbelievers' failure to worship with a call to believers to praise God.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p383/r3.anchor: فدل هذا الكلام على أنهم لا يسجدون لله تعالى، ولا يتدينون بدين، قال: ألا يا قوم أو يا مسلمون اسجدوا لله

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p384/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p384/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p384/r1.claim: In the appeal reading, ألا can address an omitted audience, or an audience after يا can be elided; Abu Zayd's poem uses ألا يا before a direct imperative.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p384/r1.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بعد يا مأمورون، فحذفوا، كما حذفوا من قوله

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p384/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p384/r2.speaker: أبو زيد
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p384/r2.claim: Abu Zayd's line ألا يا اسمع demonstrates the attention particle with an omitted or understood addressee before a command.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p384/r2.anchor: فمن ذلك ما أنشده أبو زيد : وقالت ألا يا اسمع

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p384/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p384/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p384/r3.claim: The written yāʾ in yasjudū supports the geminated أن لا reading: a light ألا would lead to asjudū without the yāʾ, whereas the verb after أن remains subjunctive with its prefix.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p384/r3.anchor: لو كانت مخففة ما كانت في يسجدوا ياء لأنها اسجدوا

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p385/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p385/r1.speaker: عاصم برواية حفص والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p385/r1.claim: Hafs from Asim and al-Kisai read the verbs with second-person tāʾ in both places.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p385/r1.anchor: فقرأ عاصم في رواية حفص والكسائي بالتاء فيهما

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p385/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p385/r2.speaker: الباقون وأبو بكر عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p385/r2.claim: The other readers, including Abu Bakr from Asim, read both verbs with third-person yāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p385/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون وأبو بكر عن عاصم بالياء فيهما

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p385/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p385/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p385/r3.claim: The yāʾ reading continues third-person narration about those led astray and God's knowledge of what they hide and reveal; the tāʾ reading follows a shift to direct address in اسجدوا لله.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p385/r3.anchor: من قرأ بالياء، فلأن الكلام على الغيبة: فزين لهم الشيطان ألا يسجدوا

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p385/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p385/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p385/r4.claim: Even after ألا يسجدوا, the verbs may address the believers and unbelievers already mentioned in third person; Abu Bakr's yāʾ best matches the third-person reading of the preceding clause.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p385/r4.anchor: ورواية أبي بكر عن عاصم [بالياء فيهما] أشبه بقراءة ألا يسجدوا

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p270#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p270#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p270#2/r1.claim: With shadda, ألا is أن plus prohibitive لا, governing the verb and dropping its nūn; it means Satan made them not prostrate to God.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p270#2/r1.anchor: جعله حرفا ناصبا للفعل ولا للنفي وأسقط النون علامة للنصب ومعناه

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p270#2/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p270#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p270#2/r2.claim: Without shadda, ألا opens the utterance; an omitted vocative yields ألا يا هؤلاء اسجدوا, as Arabic commonly does.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p270#2/r2.anchor: والحجة لمن خفف أنه جعله تنبيها واستفتاحا للكلام ثم نادى بعده

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p270#2/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p270#2/r3.speaker: عبد الله
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p270#2/r3.claim: The reading هلا يسجدون is cited as evidence for the exhortative sense, since هلا commonly urges prostration.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p270#2/r3.anchor: ودليله أنه في قراءة عبد الله هلا يسجدون وإنما تقع هلا في الكلام تحضيضا على السجود

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p270#2/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p270#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p270#2/r4.claim: ويعلم ما تخفون وما تعلنون is read with either yāʾ or tāʾ; the source says its rationale was explained earlier.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p270#2/r4.anchor: يقرآن بالياء والتاء وقد تقدم ذكر علله فيما مضى

NASHR:v2p151/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p151/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p151/r1.claim: The chapter lists ألا يسجدوا among the cases involving disagreement over separating or joining words in writing.
NASHR:v2p151/r1.anchor: وفي ألا يسجدوا فأما، ويكأن، وويكأنه وكلاهما في القصص

NASHR:v1p476/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p476/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p476/r1.claim: At pause in يخرج الخبء, the standard and regular option is نقل with bāʾ quiescent.
NASHR:v1p476/r1.anchor: فيه وجه واحد، وهو النقل مع إسكان الباء للوقف

NASHR:v1p476/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p476/r2.speaker: الحافظ أبو العلاء
NASHR:v1p476/r2.claim: Abū al-ʿAlāʾ reports an alternative, الخبا with alif, which has a possible Arabic explanation through following vowel assimilation.
NASHR:v1p476/r2.anchor: وجاء فيه وجه آخر وهو (الخبا) بالألف، ذكره الحافظ أبو العلاء

NASHR:v1p476/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p476/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p476/r3.claim: For hamza with kasra after a sound consonant, نقل is standard; rawm of the preceding rāʾ kasra is another option, also applicable to ملء, دفء, and ينظر المرء.
NASHR:v1p476/r3.anchor: ويجوز فيه وجه ثان، وهو الإشارة بالروم إلى كسرة الراء

NASHR:v1p476/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p476/r4.speaker: الهذلي
NASHR:v1p476/r4.claim: For جزء, ishmām is also available; al-Hudhalī adds idghām, but Ibn al-Jazarī says it is not soundly transmitted from Ḥamza.
NASHR:v1p476/r4.anchor: حكاه الهذلي ولا يصح عن حمزة

NASHR:v1p476/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p476/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p476/r5.claim: After an original long vowel, open hamza examples such as جيء and سيء allow نقل or idghām; both are regular options.
NASHR:v1p476/r5.anchor: فيه وجهان (الأول) النقل، وهو القياس المطرد (والثاني) الإدغام

NASHR:v1p476/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p476/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p476/r6.claim: For kasra hamza examples such as من سوء and من شيء, those two options combine with rawm, yielding four forms.
NASHR:v1p476/r6.anchor: إلا أنه يجوز مع كل الأوجه منهما الإشارة بالروم، فيصير فيها الأربعة

NASHR:v1p476/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p476/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p476/r7.claim: For ḍamma hamza examples, ishmām combines with both نقل and idghām, yielding six accepted forms; no others are sound.
NASHR:v1p476/r7.anchor: وهما الإشمام مع كل من النقل والإدغام، فيصير فيها ستة أوجه ولا يصح فيها غير ذلك

NASHR:v1p476/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p476/r8.speaker: الهذلي وابن غلبون
NASHR:v1p476/r8.claim: Deleting hamza arbitrarily, extending the preceding long vowel, or reporting bayna bayn from Ibn Ghalbūn are weak and unsound options.
NASHR:v1p476/r8.anchor: وحكى الهذلي فيه عن ابن غلبون بين بين، وكل ذلك ضعيف لا يصح، والله أعلم

QIRAAT-ER:27:25:1#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:27:25:1#1/r1.speaker: ḥf
QIRAAT-ER:27:25:1#1/r1.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and others read hamza plus lā as a separate exhortative particle, rather than the merged anna plus lā.
QIRAAT-ER:27:25:1#1/r1.anchor: ḥf, mutawatir: Alternative reading by al-Kisāʾī and others: hamza + lā as separate exhortative particle

QIRAAT-ER:27:25:1#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:27:25:1#2/r1.speaker: al-Kisāʾī
QIRAAT-ER:27:25:1#2/r1.claim: Al-Kisāʾī parses alā as an exhortation, yā as vocative, and usjudū as imperative: “Indeed! O, prostrate!”
QIRAAT-ER:27:25:1#2/r1.anchor: al-Kisāʾī: exhortative a-lā + vocative yā + imperative usjudū — transforms the clause into a direct command

QIRAAT-ER:27:25:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:27:25:2#1/r1.speaker: al-Kisāʾī
QIRAAT-ER:27:25:2#1/r1.claim: Al-Kisāʾī splits yasjudū into vocative yā and imperative usjudū, changing the mood from subjunctive to imperative.
QIRAAT-ER:27:25:2#1/r1.anchor: al-Kisāʾī: reanalysis splits yasjudū into vocative yā + imperative usjudū — changes mood from subjunctive

QIRAAT-ER:27:25:7#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:27:25:7#1/r1.speaker: waqf
QIRAAT-ER:27:25:7#1/r1.claim: The pausal form has sukūn on bāʾ before hamza and preserves the consonantal skeleton.
QIRAAT-ER:27:25:7#1/r1.anchor: waqf, mutawatir: Pausal form with sukūn on bāʾ before hamza — waqf reading preserving the consonantal skeleton

QIRAAT-ER:27:25:15#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:27:25:15#1/r1.speaker: Imp
QIRAAT-ER:27:25:15#1/r1.claim: Third-person yukhfūna removes the shift from third to second person and keeps both concealment and declaration consistently in third person.
QIRAAT-ER:27:25:15#1/r1.anchor: Imp, mutawatir: "3rd person: ""what they conceal and what they declare"" — eliminates the person-shift

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p81/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p81/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p81/r1.claim: Qatada glosses the hidden thing as a secret.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p81/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ الذي يخرج الخبء ﴾ قال هو السر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r1.claim: Because God taught the hoopoe to detect hidden water, it fittingly describes Him as bringing hidden things forth; specialist knowledge shows in manner and speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r1.anchor: كان الهدهد قد أوتي من معرفة الماء تحت الأرض ما لم يؤت غيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r2.claim: A report says God clothes every servant with the mantle of the work he performs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r2.anchor: ما عمل عبد عملا إلا ألقى الله عليه رداء عمله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r3.speaker: الحرميان والجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r3.claim: The Ḥaramī readers and majority use third-person verbs referring to the queen and her people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحرميان والجمهور: ما يخفون وما يعلنون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r4.speaker: الكسائي وحفص
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r4.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and Ḥafṣ use second-person address, possibly to Solomon and attendants.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r5.claim: The hoopoe could address Solomon's attendants too; it had already said it encompassed what Solomon did not.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r6.claim: The apparent reading makes these words part of the hoopoe's speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r6.anchor: ألا يسجدوا إلى العظيم من كلام الهدهد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r7.claim: Another view takes them as God's address to Muḥammad's community.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r7.anchor: من كلام الله تعالى لأمة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says third person indicates the hoopoe's speech and second person God's address.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p231/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: القراءة بياء الغيبة تعطي أن الآية من كلام الهدهد

ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r1.claim: الخبء is a verbal noun used here for anything concealed in the heavens or earth, whatever it may be.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r1.anchor: أي يظهر الشيء المخبوء فيهما كائنا ما كان فالخبء مصدر أريد به اسم المفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r2.claim: Some interpret the hidden thing here specifically as rain and vegetation; Ibn Zayd is cited for this view.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r2.anchor: وفسره بعضهم هنا بالمطر والنبات وروي ذلك عن ابن زيد

ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r3.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r3.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim transmits that Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab interpreted the hidden thing as water.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن سعيد بن المسيب أنه فسره بالماء

ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r4.claim: Al-Alusi prefers the general sense of anything concealed, as transmitted from a group of authorities from Ibn Abbas.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r4.anchor: والاولى التعميم كما روي ذلك عن جماعة عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r5.claim: The prepositional phrase modifies الخبء; al-Farra instead takes في to mean من and attaches the phrase to يخرج, but Al-Alusi prefers the apparent construction.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r5.anchor: ( وفي السموات ) متعلق بالخبء وعن الفراء

ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r6.claim: This divine attribute suits the story because it reveals what is hidden, like the disclosure of Bilqis and her affairs; the choice of the following attributes likewise fits the story.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r6.anchor: واختيار هذا الوصف لما أنه أوفق بالقصة حيث تضمنت ما هو أشبه شيء باخراج الخبء وهو إظهار أمر بلقيس

ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r7.claim: One explanation says the hoopoe especially grasped this attribute by witnessing God's signs, including a God-given capacity to locate water underground.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r7.anchor: وقيل : إن تخصيص هذا الوصف بالذكر لما أن الهدهد أرسخ في معرفته والاحاطة باحكامه بمشاهدة ءاثاره

ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r8.claim: Al-Alusi rejects the hoopoe explanation as unsupported by any reliable report; it also fails to fit the light reading ألا يسجدوا when understood as a fresh statement from God or Solomon.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r8.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن كون الهدهد أودع فيه القدرة على ما ذكر مما لم يجيء فيه خبر يعول عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas and the six readers are cited for reading ألا يسجدوا without doubling the jīm; on an independent-speech construction, the words are spoken by God or Solomon.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r9.anchor: على قراءة ابن عباس والستة والذين معه ( ألا يسجدوا ) بالتخفيف إذا جعل الكلام استئنافا من جهته عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r10.claim: Al-Alusi begins to note a point made by coordinating the statement about what people conceal and reveal, but the surviving excerpt ends before completing the explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192/r10.anchor: وأشير بعطف قوله تعالى ( ويعلم ما تخفون وما تعلنون

ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r1.claim: God brings hidden realities in the human world to light just as He brings concealed things in the greater world to light, exposing hidden states for recompense.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r1.anchor: أنه تعالى يخرج ما في العالم الانساني من الخفايا كما يخرج ما في العالم الكبير

ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r2.claim: God reveals the concealed conditions people hide so He can requite them; mentioning what they disclose broadens the scope of His knowledge or stresses that hidden and open are equal to Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r2.anchor: يظهر ما تخفونه من الأحوال فيجازيكم بها وذكر ماتعلنون لتوسيع دائرة العلم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r3.claim: Some infer that the earlier description points to God's complete power, while this description points to His complete knowledge, in which hidden and apparent are equal.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r3.anchor: كلام بعضهم يانه أشير بما تقدم إلى كمال قدرته تعالى وبهذا إلى كمال علمه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r4.claim: The concealed is mentioned before the disclosed because it suits the preceding mention of hidden things and signals that both are equally known; bringing forth hidden things from heaven comes first because it better fits the context.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r4.anchor: وقدم ( ماتخفون ) لذلك مع مناسبته لما قبله من الخبء وقدم وصفه تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r5.claim: The address may be directed to people generally, Solomon's people, or Bilqis's people.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r5.anchor: والخطاب على ما قيل اما للناس أو لقوم سليمان أو لقوم بلقيس

ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r6.claim: The passage contains a shift in grammatical person (iltifāt).

ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r7.speaker: الحرميان والجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r7.claim: The two canonical readers of the Ḥaram and the majority read the verbs in the third person: what they conceal and disclose.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ الحرميان والجمهور ( مايخفون وما يعلنون ) بياء الغيبة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r8.speaker: أبي
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r8.claim: Ubayy has a variant reading addressing the hearers directly and ending with God's knowledge of their secret and what they disclose.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p192#2/r8.anchor: وفي الكشاف عن أبي أنه قرأ ( ألاتسجدون لله الذي يخرج الخبء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر والكسائي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r1.claim: Abu Jaʿfar and al-Kisaʾi lighten ألا يسجدوا; at pause they read ألا يا, then begin اسجدوا as a fresh divine command to people.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر والكسائي: "ألا يسجدوا" بالتخفيف، وإذا وقفوا يقفون "ألا يا": ألا يا ثم يبتدئون: "اسجدوا"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r2.claim: On the light reading, يا implies the omitted هؤلاء; ألا is an intervening phrase spoken either by the hoopoe or Solomon.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r2.anchor: وحذفوا هؤلاء اكتفاء بدلالة "يا" عليها، وذكر بعضهم سماعا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r3.claim: Arab usage supports omitting the vocative after يا, as in ألا يا ارحمونا; al-Akhtal likewise addresses Hind with ألا يا اسلمي.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r3.anchor: وذكر بعضهم سماعا من العرب: ألا يا ارحمونا، يريدون ألا يا قوم، وقال الأخطل: ألا يا اسلمي يا هند

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r4.speaker: الآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r4.claim: Other readers stress ألا, meaning Satan adorned their deeds so they would not prostrate to God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون: "ألا يسجدوا" بالتشديد، بمعنى: وزين لهم الشيطان أعمالهم لئلا يسجدوا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r5.claim: Al-khabʾ is something hidden; most exegetes identify heaven’s hidden thing as rain and earth’s as vegetation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r5.anchor: أي: الخفي المخبأ، {في السموات والأرض} أي: ما خبأت. قال أكثر المفسرين: خبء السماء: المطر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r6.speaker: عبد الله
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r6.claim: The reading attributed to ʿAbd Allah has من rather than في; Arabic can use في and من interchangeably.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r6.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله: "يخرج الخبء من السموات والأرض"، و"من" و"في" يتعاقبان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r7.claim: Another gloss takes khabʾ as the unseen of the heavens and earth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: معنى "الخبء" الغيب، يريد: يعلم غيب السموات والأرض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r8.speaker: الكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r8.claim: Al-Kisaʾi and Hafs from ʿAsim read both verbs with second-person تاء; the others read them with ياء.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p156#2/r8.anchor: قرأ الكسائي، وحفص، عن عاصم: بالتاء فيهما، لأن أول الآية خطاب على قراءة الكسائي

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r6.claim: Allā yasjudū may mean Satan blocked them lest they prostrate or adorned their refusal; alternatively, they fail to find the way to prostration with an extra lā.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r6.anchor: فصدهم لئلا يسجدوا أو زين لهم أن لا يسجدوا

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r7.speaker: الكسائي ويعقوب
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r7.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and Yaʿqūb read illā with a light hamza as a call to attention, with an omitted addressee: O people, prostrate.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r7.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي ويعقوب { إلا } بالتخفيف على أنها للتنبيه ويا للنداء

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r8.claim: The light reading permits a new divine or Solomonic command after a pause at lā yahtadūn; the other rebukes refusal, and both imply prostration is obligatory generally, not necessarily on recitation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r8.anchor: وعلى هذا صح أن يكون استئنافا من الله أو من سليمان

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r9.claim: Other readings include halā with hamza changed to hāʾ and direct-address forms alā tasjudūn and halā tasjudūn.

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r10.claim: The cited poetic line illustrates the attention-getting vocative construction.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r10.anchor: وقالت ألا يا اسمع أعظك بخطة

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r11.claim: Khabʾ is something hidden within another; bringing it out means revealing it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r11.anchor: و { الخبء } ما خفي في غيره وإخراجه إظهاره

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r12.claim: God brings forth shining stars, falling rain, sprouting plants, creation actualized from potential, and origination from possibility and nonexistence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r12.anchor: وهو يعم إشراق الكواكب وإنزال الأمطار وإنبات النبات

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r13.claim: Only the Necessary Existent has power to bring things from possibility and nonexistence into existence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r13.anchor: ما في الإمكان والعدم إلى الوجوب والوجود

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r14.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r14.claim: God's perfect power and knowledge entitle Him alone to worship, urging prostration and refuting worship of others.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r14.anchor: بما يوجب اختصاصه باستحقاق السجود من التفرد

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r15.speaker: حفص والكسائي
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r15.claim: Ḥafṣ and al-Kisāʾī read the verbs with tāʾ, addressing listeners directly.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:23-25/r15.anchor: وقرأ حفص والكسائي »ما تخفون وما تعلنون« بالتاء

BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r1.claim: The hoopoe marvels that a people governed by political order and reason lack prostration, the greatest act that draws a person near to God.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r1.anchor: علله بانتفاء أعظم مقرب إلى الله : السجود , تعظيما له وتنويها به فقال

BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r2.claim: One analysis connects ‘so that they do not prostrate’ to their blindness: the devil’s dominion over them followed from their lack of prostration.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r2.anchor: أي حصل لهم هذا العمى العظيم الذي استولى به عليهم الشيطان لانتفاء سجودهم , ويجوز أن يتعلق بالتزيين

BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r3.claim: Alternatively, the clause attaches to Satan’s beautifying their deeds, which was intended to keep them from prostrating.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يتعلق بالتزيين , اي زين لهم لئلا يسجدوا { لله } أي يعبدوا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r4.claim: Prostration is worship, nearness, and intimate address to God; had they prayed, they would have been guided, since prayer restrains indecency and wrongdoing.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r4.anchor: فإنهم لو سجدوا له سبحانه لاهتدوا , فإن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر ,

BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r5.speaker: الكسائي وأبو جعفر
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r5.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and Abū Jaʿfar read the verb lightly, with an extended fatḥa on yāʾ, as a fresh exhortatory sentence.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r5.anchor: وعلى قراءة الكسائي وأبي جعفر بالتخفيف وإشباع فتح الياء يكون استئنافا , بدىء بأداة الاستفتاح

BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r6.claim: On that reading, an implied direct address—‘O these people, prostrate to God’—is omitted because the situation is urgent and punishment may come swiftly.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r6.anchor: ثم نادى لمثل ذلك وحذف المنادى إيذانا بالاكتفاء بالإشارة لضيق الحال , خوفا من المبادرة بالنكال

BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r7.claim: Khabʾ is something already hidden inside something else, such as water underground, or something hidden potentially that does not yet exist.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r7.anchor: وهوالشيء المخبوء بالفعل المخفي في غيره , وهو ما وجد وغيب عن الخلق كالماء الذي في بطن الأرض , أو بالقوة وهو ما لم يوجد أصلا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r8.claim: He singles out heaven and earth as the bounds of human observation, where clouds, rain, plants, celestial bodies, weather, movement, and stillness emerge into sight.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r8.anchor: وخصه بقوله : { في السماوات والأرض } لأن ذلك منتهى مشاهدتنا , فننظر ما يتكون فيهما بعد أن لم يكن من سحاب ومطر ونبات

BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r9.claim: God brings what is hidden in the unseen into the visible world; the secret thoughts people conceal are more hidden than things detectable by signs.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r9.anchor: والمعنى أنه يخرج ما هو في عالم الغيب فيجعله في عالم الشهادة . ولما كان ذلك قد يخص بما لم يضمر في القلوب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r10.claim: Knowledge of what people conceal entails knowledge of what they declare; God states the latter explicitly despite the noise and overlap that may obscure public speech.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421/r10.anchor: وكان التصريح ما ليس لغيره من المكنة والطمأنينة

DURR-FULL:v6p351/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p351/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p351/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the hidden thing as every secret in heaven and earth, which God knows.
DURR-FULL:v6p351/r14.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {يخرج الخبء} قال: يعلم كل خفية في السماء والأرض

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God brings out every hidden thing in the heavens and earth.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : يخرج الخبء في السماوات والأرض يعلم كل خفية في السماوات و الأرض

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r2.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r2.claim: ʿIkrima glosses al-khabʾ as a secret.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله : يخرج الخبء في السماوات والأرض قال الخبء السر

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r3.claim: Mujahid glosses al-khabʾ as the unseen.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : يخرج الخبء الغيب

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r4.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr is reported to share ʿIkrima's gloss of al-khabʾ as a secret.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r4.anchor: روي عن سعيد بن جبير وقتادة مثل قول عكرمة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r5.claim: Qatada is reported to share ʿIkrima's gloss of al-khabʾ as a secret.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r5.anchor: روي عن سعيد بن جبير وقتادة مثل قول عكرمة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r6.claim: In another report, Mujahid glosses al-khabʾ as rain.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : يخرج الخبء قال : الغيث

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r7.speaker: حكيم بن جابر
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r7.claim: Ḥakīm ibn Jābir is also reported to explain al-khabʾ as rain.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r7.anchor: عن حكيم بن جابر انه الغيث

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r8.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r8.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib says al-khabʾ is water.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r8.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب انه سئل ، عن قوله : يخرج الخبء قال : الخبء الماء

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r9.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r9.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd explains the hidden provision in heaven and earth as what God placed there: provision, rain from heaven, and plants from earth.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r9.anchor: سمعت عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم في قول الله الذي يخرج الخبء في السماوات والأرض قال : خبء السماوات

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God knows what people do by night and by day.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : ويعلم ما تخفون وما تعلنون يقول : يعلم ما عملوا بالليل والنهار

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r11.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r11.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r11.claim: Al-Ḥasan says God knows what they conceal in the dark of night and inside their homes.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2868/r11.anchor: عن الحسن يعلم ما تخفون وما تعلنون قال في ظلمة الليل ، وفي اجواف بيوتهم

BURSEVI:v6p247#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p247#4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p247#4/r2.claim: The phrase is the object of purpose after an omitted lām: Satan turned them away so they would not prostrate.
BURSEVI:v6p247#4/r2.anchor: مفعول له للصد على حذف اللام منه أي فسدهم لئلا يسجدوا

BURSEVI:v6p247#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p247#4/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p247#4/r3.claim: The phrase censures their failure to prostrate, which is why prostration is required at the end of these verses.
BURSEVI:v6p247#4/r3.anchor: وهو ذم لهم على ترك السجود فلذا وجب السجود عند تمام هذه الآيات

BURSEVI:v6p247#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p247#4/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p247#4/r4.claim: Khabʾ is something stored and concealed; God brings forth hidden things in heaven and earth, such as snow, rain, plants, and water.
BURSEVI:v6p247#4/r4.anchor: الخبأ يقال للمدخر المستور أي يظهر ما هو مخبوء ومخفي فيها كائنا ماكان

BURSEVI:v6p247#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p247#4/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p247#4/r5.claim: The hidden refers to what hearts conceal and the manifest to what tongues and limbs disclose; mentioning both broadens the scope and stresses equal divine knowledge.
BURSEVI:v6p247#4/r5.anchor: بالألسنة والجوارح وذكر ما تعلنون لتوسيع دائرة العلم للتنبيه على تساويهما

BURSEVI:v6p247#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p247#4/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p247#4/r6.claim: The Persian couplet says not even a grain is hidden from God's knowledge; the concealed and manifest are alike to Him.
BURSEVI:v6p247#4/r6.anchor: برو علم يك ذره وشيده نيست كه نهان ويدا بنزدش يكيست

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r1.claim: Poetic examples show ألا as a call of attention; the intensified reading may prompt, with an implicit call afterward, though this requires ellipsis.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r1.anchor: ويحتمل قراءة من شدد: «ألا» أن يجعلها بمعنى التخصيص، ويقدر هذا النداء بعدها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r3.claim: Ibn Masud's codex has ألا هل تسجدون with second-person ت.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r3.anchor: وفي حرف عبد الله بن مسعود «ألا هل تسجدون» بالتاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r4.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r4.claim: Ubay's reading is ألا هل تسجدوا, also with second-person ت.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r4.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي: «ألا هل تسجدوا» بالتاء أيضا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r5.claim: Khabʾ is hidden; the sky's hidden provision is rain, earth's treasures and vegetation, and the word extends to any hidden thing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r5.anchor: والخبء الخفي من الأمور وهو من خبأت الشيء، و «خبء» السماء مطرها، و «خبء» الأرض كنوزها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets khabʾ broadly as anything hidden.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r6.anchor: واللفظة بعد هذا تعم كل خفي من الأمور وبه فسر ابن عباس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r7.speaker: الجمهور وأبي بن كعب وعكرمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r7.claim: Most retain silent b and hamza; Ubay reads al-khab with open b and no hamza; Ikrima reads al-khaba with shortened alif.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «الخبء» بسكون الباء والهمز، وقرأ أبي بن كعب «الخب» بفتح الباء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r8.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r8.claim: Sibawayh says some Arabs replace hamza after a quiescent consonant with alif, waw, or ya according to its vowel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r8.anchor: وحكى سيبويه أن بعض العرب يقلب الهمزة إذا كانت في مثل هذا مفتوحة وقبلها ساكن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r9.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r9.claim: Most read the verbs in third person, which Ibn Atiyya says makes the verse part of the hoopoe's speech.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ جمهور القراء «يخفون» و «يعلنون» بياء الغائب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r10.speaker: الكسائي وعاصم في رواية حفص
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r10.claim: They read the verbs in second person, making the verse God's address to Muhammad's community.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي وعاصم في رواية حفص «تخفون وما تعلنون» بتاء الخطاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r11.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r11.claim: Ubay's codex expands the phrase as والله الذي يخرج الخبء and refers to what you conceal as your secret.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r11.anchor: والله الذي يخرج الخبء من السماوات والأرض ويعلم سركم وما تعلنون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r1.speaker: الأكثرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r1.claim: Most readers double the lām; the phrase means Satan prevented them from prostrating to God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r1.anchor: قرأ الأكثرون ألا بالتشديد قال الزجاج والمعنى وزين لهم الشيطان ألا يسجدوا أي فصدهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو عبد الرحمن السلمي والحسن والزهري وقتادة وأبو العالية وحميد الأعرج والأعمش وابن أبي عبلة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r2.claim: These readers lighten the lām and understand the phrase as an address: Well then, you people, prostrate; the vocative is elided, with a pause after alā yā.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وابو عبد الرحمن السلمي والحسن والزهري وقتادة وأبو العالية وحميد الأعرج والأعمش وابن أبي عبلة والكسائي ألا يسجدوا مخففة على معنى ألا يا هؤلاء اسجدوا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r3.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r3.claim: On the light reading, al-Farra counts it as a prostration verse; on the doubled reading it should not be treated as one.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r3.anchor: قال الفراء فعلى هذه القراءة هي سجدة وعلى قراءة من شدد لا ينبغي لها أن تكون سجدة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r4.claim: Abu ʿUbayda takes the light reading as a fresh divine command: O people, prostrate.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة هذا أمر من الله مستأنف يعني ألا يا أيها الناس اسجدوا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿud and Ubayy read hal yasjudū, with hāʾ instead.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وأبي هلا يسجدوا بهاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r6.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r6.claim: Ibn Qutayba says al-khabʾ is what is concealed: rain is the hidden thing in heaven and plants are the hidden thing in earth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r6.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة أي المستتر فيهما وهو من خبأت الشيء إذا أخفيته ويقال خبء السموات المطر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj says anything concealed is khabʾ, so the phrase means that God knows the unseen in heaven and earth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r7.anchor: وقال الزجاج كل ما خبأته فهو خبء فالخبء كل ما غاب فالمعنى يعلم الغيب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r8.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r8.claim: Ibn Jarir takes fī to mean min, so the phrase means bringing forth what is hidden from the heavens.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166/r8.anchor: وقال ابن جرير في بمعنى من فتقديره يخرج الخبء من السموات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166#2/r1.speaker: حفص عن عاصم والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166#2/r1.claim: Hafs from ʿAsim and al-Kisaʾi read both verbs in the second person; the rest read them in the third person.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166#2/r1.anchor: قرأ حفص عن عاصم والكسائي بالتاء فيهما وقرأ الباقون بالياء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166#2/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166#2/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says the hoopoe speaks from the words I encompassed through the words the Great.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p166#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد من قوله أحطت إلى قوله العظيم كلام الهدهد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187/r1.claim: The phrase continues that Satan adorned their deeds and turned them from the way: they do not know the true path of worshipping God alone rather than created stars and other things; see 41:37.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187/r1.anchor: لا يعرفون سبيل الحق التي هي إخلاص السجود لله وحده دون ما خلق من شيء من الكواكب وغيرها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187/r2.speaker: بعض القراء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187/r2.claim: Some reciters read alā yā usjudū lillāh, treating alā as an opening particle and yā as a vocative with an omitted addressee, estimated as O people, prostrate to God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187/r2.anchor: وقرأ بعض القراء: "ألا يا اسجدوا لله" جعلها "ألا" الاستفتاحية، و"يا" للنداء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ali ibn Abi Talha, and Ikrima, Mujahid, Said ibn Jubayr, Qatada, and others say al-khabʾ means every hidden thing in heaven and earth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187/r3.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: يعلم كل خبيئة في السماء والأرض

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187/r4.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187/r4.claim: Said ibn al-Musayyib interprets al-khabʾ as water.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187/r4.anchor: وقال سعيد بن المسيب: الخبء: الماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187/r5.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187/r5.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam interprets the hidden provision of heaven and earth as rain from heaven and plants from earth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187/r5.anchor: وكذا قال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم: خبء السموات والأرض: ما جعل فيها من الأرزاق: المطر من السماء، والنبات من الأرض

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187/r6.claim: This fits the hoopoe’s special ability, reported from Ibn Abbas and others, to see water flowing in the depths and interior of the earth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187/r6.anchor: وهذا مناسب من كلام الهدهد، الذي جعل الله فيه من الخاصية ما ذكره ابن عباس وغيره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187#2/r1.claim: God knows what servants conceal and reveal in words and deeds, as in 13:10.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187#2/r1.anchor: أي: يعلم ما يخفيه العباد، وما يعلنونه من الأقوال والأفعال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187#2/r3.claim: Because the hoopoe called people to good and worship of God alone, killing it was forbidden; Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet prohibited killing four creatures—ant, bee, hoopoe, and shrike—and Ibn Kathir grades the chain sound.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p187#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، قال: نهى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن قتل أربع من الدواب

JISHUMI:v8p5418/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5418/r10.speaker: السلمي والحسن وأبو جعفر وحميد والكسائي ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v8p5418/r10.claim: These readers lighten allā as a fresh divine command to prostrate, eliding hāʾulāʾ as indicated by yāʾ.
JISHUMI:v8p5418/r10.anchor: قرأ السلمي والحسن وأبو جعفر وحميد والكسائي ويعقوب: ألا يسجدوا بالتخفيف على تقدير: يا هؤلاء اسجدوا،

JISHUMI:v8p5418/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5418/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5418/r11.claim: The elided hāʾulāʾ is indicated by yāʾ, as in the cited line to Hind.
JISHUMI:v8p5418/r11.anchor: وحذفوا (هؤلاء) اكتفاء بدلالة يا عليها كقول الشاعر: ألا يا اسلمي يا هند هند بني بدر

JISHUMI:v8p5418/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5418/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5418/r12.claim: On the light reading, isjudū is a jussive imperative; pause after yā and resume at isjudū.
JISHUMI:v8p5418/r12.anchor: فعلى هذا (اسجدوا) جزم؛ لأنه أمر، وإذا وقف عليه قال: (ألا يا) ثم يبتدئ: اسجدوا.

JISHUMI:v8p5418/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5418/r13.speaker: الباقون
JISHUMI:v8p5418/r13.claim: Other readers geminate allā, parsed as li-allā with subjunctive yasjudū; pause after allā and resume at yasjudū.
JISHUMI:v8p5418/r13.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: ألا يسجدوا بتشديد (ألا)، وقيل في تقديره: لئلا يسجدوا، ف (أن) في موضع نصب،

JISHUMI:v8p5418/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5418/r14.speaker: أبو عبيد
JISHUMI:v8p5418/r14.claim: Abū ʿUbayd prefers gemination: lightening is plausible but breaks the link to Sheba, while gemination preserves continuity.
JISHUMI:v8p5418/r14.anchor: واختار أبو عبيد التشديد وقال: للتخفيف وجه حسن إلا أن فيه انقطاع الخبر عن أمر سبأ،

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r20.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r20.claim: Ikrimah, Mujahid, Qatada, and Ibn Jubayr interpret the hidden thing as what is unseen in the heavens and earth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r20.anchor: غيب السموات والأرض ، قاله عكرمة ، ومجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r21.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r21.claim: Ibn Zayd says the hidden thing in heaven is rain and the hidden thing on earth is vegetation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r21.anchor: أن خبء السموات المطر وخبء الأرض النبات ، قاله ابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r22.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r22.claim: Al-Mawardi says khabʾ can mean something absent or concealed; the verbal noun khabʾ is used in place of the passive participle as a description.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r22.anchor: والخبء بمعنى المخبوء وقع المصدر موقع الصفة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r23.speaker: الكسائي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r23.claim: Al-Kisa'i reads ألا يسجدوا with a light form; the other readers use the doubled form.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r23.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي { ألا يسجدوا } بالتخفيف وقرأ الباقون بالتشديد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r24.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r24.claim: Al-Farra says the light reading marks a prostration place, while the doubled reading does not.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r24.anchor: قال الفراء : من قرأ بالتخفيف فهو موضع سجدة , ومن قرأ بالتشديد فليس بموضع سجدة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r25.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r25.claim: One account makes the words God's command to all creatures to prostrate, paraphrased as “O people, prostrate to God.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r25.anchor: أحدهما : أنه قول الله تعالى أمر فيه بالسجود له , وهو أمر منه لجميع خلقه

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r26.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r26.claim: The alternative is that these are the hoopoe’s words, reported by God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r26.anchor: الثاني : أنه قول الهدهد حكاه الله عنه

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r27.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r27.claim: On the hoopoe-speech account, it may have addressed Bilqis’s people after finding them prostrating to other than God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r27.anchor: أحدهما : أن يكون قاله لقوم بلقيس حين وجدهم يسجدون لغير الله

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r28.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r28.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r28.claim: Alternatively, the hoopoe may have said this to Solomon on its return, expressing disapproval of what it found.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r28.anchor: الثاني : أن يكون قاله لسليمان عند عوده إليه واستكبارا لما وجدهم عليه

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r29.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r29.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r29.claim: One rationale says the hoopoe understood from the inspiration to obey Solomon that he was a prophet whose words and actions must be obeyed, even if the bird was not legally accountable.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r29.anchor: أنه وإن يكن ممن قد علم وجوب التكليف بالفعل فهو ممن قد تصور بما ألهم من الطاعة لسليمان أنه نبي مطاع لا يخالف في قول ولا عمل

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r30.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r30.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r30.claim: Another rationale compares the hoopoe to a child nearing maturity who sees people worship God and recognizes contrary worship as false.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p203/r30.anchor: أنه كالصبي منا إذا راهق فرآنا على عبادة الله تصور أن ما خالفها باطل فكذا الهدهد في تصوره أن ما خالف فعل سليمان باطل

MUJAHID:v2p471/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p471/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p471/r1.claim: What God brings forth from concealment is rain.
MUJAHID:v2p471/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ يخرج الخبء ﴾ قال يخرج الغيث

MUQATIL:27:21-26/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:27:21-26/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:27:21-26/r9.claim: The hoopoe urges them to prostrate to God, who brings hidden rain from the heavens and earth.
MUQATIL:27:21-26/r9.anchor: ألا يسجدوا لله الذي يخرج الخبء } يعنى الغيث { في السماوات والأرض

MUQATIL:27:21-26/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:27:21-26/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:27:21-26/r10.claim: God knows what they conceal in their hearts and what they declare with their tongues.
MUQATIL:27:21-26/r10.anchor: ويعلم ما تخفون } فى قلوبكم { وما تعلنون } [آية: 25] بألسنتكم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r1.claim: With gemination, the phrase means Satan turned them from the way so they would not prostrate; the preposition before an is omitted and nun assimilated into lam. Another parse makes la extra.
