NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r1.anchor: بالتشديد أي فصدهم عن السبيل لئلا يسجدوا فحذف الجار مع أن وادغمت النون في اللام ويجوز أن تكون لا مزيدة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r2.claim: With the light reading it can mean Pay attention, you people, prostrate; ala marks attention, ya is vocative, and the person addressed is omitted.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r2.anchor: وبالتخفيف يزيد وعلى تقديره ألا يا هؤلاء اسجدوا فألا للتنبيه ويا حرف نداء ومناداه محدوف

NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r3.claim: The geminated reading permits a pause only at the mighty throne; the light reading permits pauses after they are not guided or before the command.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r3.anchor: فمن شدد لم يقف إلا على العرش العظيم ومن خفف وقف على فهم لا يهتدون ثم ابتدأ ألا يسجدوا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r4.claim: Prostration of recitation is obligatory with both readings: one commands it and the other censures those who leave it.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r4.anchor: وسجدة التلاوة واجبة في القراءتين جميعا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r5.speaker: الزجاج
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj says prostration is not obligatory with gemination; Nasafi rejects this because the verse censures the one who leaves it.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r5.anchor: بخلاف ما يقوله الزجاج أنه لا يجب السجود مع التشديد لأن مواضع السجدة إما أمر بها أو مدح أو ذم لتاركها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r6.claim: The hidden thing is named by the verbal noun for hiding.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r6.anchor: ﴿ لله الذي يخرج الخبء ﴾ سمي المخبوء بالمصدر

NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r7.speaker: قتادة
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r7.claim: Qatada explains heaven's hidden treasure as rain and earth's as plants.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r7.anchor: قتادة خبء السماء المطر وخبء الأرض النبات

NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r8.speaker: حفص
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210/r8.claim: Hafs reads both verbs with ta, addressing the listeners.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو ونافع وعاصم وحمزة
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r5.claim: Abū ʿAmr, Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim, and Ḥamza read allā with a doubled lām.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r5.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو ونافع وعاصم وحمزة: { ألا يسجدوا لله } بتشديد { ألا }

QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r6.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says the preceding clause cannot end at fahum lā yahtadūn on the doubled reading, because the meaning continues with Satan adorning their failure to prostrate.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r6.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: { فهم لا يهتدون } غير تام لمن شدد { ألا }

QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r7.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r7.claim: Al-Akhfash parses an as governed by zayyana, meaning Satan adorned their deeds so that they would not prostrate.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r7.anchor: قال الأخفش: ب { زين } أي وزين لهم لئلا يسجدوا لله.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r8.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r8.claim: Al-Kisāʾī attaches an to faṣaddahum: Satan turned them away from prostrating.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r8.anchor: وقال الكسائي: ب { فصدهم } أي فصدهم ألا يسجدوا. وهو في الوجهين مفعول له.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r9.speaker: اليزيدي وعلي بن سليمان
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r9.claim: Al-Yazīdī and ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān parse an as an accusative substitute for aʿmālahum.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r9.anchor: وقال اليزيدي وعلي بن سليمان: { أن } بدل من { أعمالهم } في موضع نصب.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r10.claim: Abū ʿAmr parses an in the genitive as a substitute for al-sabīl.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r10.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو: و { أن } في موضع خفض على البدل من السبيل.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r11.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r11.claim: Another analysis attaches the clause to lā yahtadūn: they are not guided to know prostration is obligatory; on this view lā is extra.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r11.anchor: وقيل العامل فيها { لا يهتدون } أي فهم لا يهتدون أن يسجدوا لله

QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r12.claim: On the doubled reading this reports their failure to prostrate, through adornment, diversion, or lack of guidance, so it is not a place for prostration of recitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r12.anchor: وعلى هذه القراءة فليس بموضع سجدة لأن ذلك خبر عنهم بترك السجود، إما بالتزيين، أو بالصد، أو بمنع الاهتداء.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r13.speaker: الزهري والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r13.claim: Al-Zuhrī, al-Kisāʾī, and others read it as a vocative phrase, allā yā hāʾulāʾ, followed by the command asjudū.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r13.anchor: وقرأ الزهري والكسائي وغيرهما: { ألا يسجدوا لله } بمعنى ألا يا هؤلاء اسجدوا

QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r14.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r14.claim: Sībawayh says yā addresses the omitted people, not the curse in his cited line.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r14.anchor: قال سيبويه: يا لغير اللعنة، لأنه لو كان للعنة لنصبها

QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r15.claim: Arabic usage includes allā yā followed by commands, with an omitted vocative such as yā qawm; on this reading asjudū is jussive after a pause.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r15.anchor: وحكى بعضهم سماعا عن العرب: ألا يا ارحموا ألا يا اصدقوا. يريدون ألا يا قوم ارحموا اصدقوا

QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r16.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r16.claim: Al-Kisāʾī says he heard the elders read only the light form, construing it as a command.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r16.anchor: قال الكسائي: ما كنت أسمع الأشياخ يقرؤونها إلا بالتخفيف على نية الأمر.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r17.speaker: عبد الله وأبي
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r17.claim: The readings attributed to ʿAbd Allāh and Ubayy, both with an address to prostrate, support the light reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r17.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله: { ألا هل تسجدون لله } بالتاء والنون. وفي قراءة أبي «ألا تسجدون لله» فهاتان القراءتان حجة لمن خفف.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r18.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r18.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the light reading makes prostration obligatory, unlike the doubled reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r18.anchor: الزجاج: وقراءة التخفيف تقتضي وجوب السجود دون التشديد.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r19.speaker: أبو حاتم وأبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r19.claim: Abū Ḥātim and Abū ʿUbayd prefer the doubled reading because it keeps the account of Saba continuous; the light reading interrupts it.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r19.anchor: واختار أبو حاتم وأبو عبيدة قراءة التشديد. وقال: التخفيف وجه حسن إلا أن فيه انقطاع الخبر من أمر سبأ، ثم رجع بعد إلى ذكرهم،

QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r20.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r20.claim: Al-Naḥḥās calls the light reading remote because it interrupts the passage, while the doubled reading keeps it connected.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r20.anchor: ونحوه قال النحاس قال: قراءة التخفيف بعيدة لأن الكلام يكون معترضا، وقراءة التشديد يكون الكلام بها متسقا

QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r21.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r21.claim: Al-Naḥḥās adds that the written form would require deleting two alifs rather than the usual one, as in yā ʿĪsā ibn Maryam.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:24-25/r21.anchor: وأيضا فإن السواد على غير هذه القراءة لأنه قد حذف منها ألفان، وإنما يختصر مثل هذا بحذف ألف واحدة نحو يا عيسى ابن مريم.

QASHANI:27:25-27/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:27:25-27/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:27:25-27/r1.claim: They were turned from the path so they would not submit and bring their potential perfections into actuality in the intellect.
QASHANI:27:25-27/r1.anchor: فصدهم عن السبيل لئلا ينقادوا ويذعنوا في إخراج كمالاتهم إلى العقل

QASHANI:27:25-27/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:27:25-27/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:27:25-27/r2.claim: The hidden treasure is possible perfection concealed in the heavens of spirits and the earth of the body.
QASHANI:27:25-27/r2.anchor: المخبوء من الكمالات الممكنة في سموات الأرواح وأرض الجسم

QASHANI:27:25-27/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:27:25-27/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:27:25-27/r3.claim: God knows latent perfections blocked from intellect by veiling actions as well as the dark dispositions and ruinous morals people manifest.
QASHANI:27:25-27/r3.anchor: مما فيهم بالقوة من الكمالات بالأعمال الحاجبة والمانعة لخروج ما في الاستعداد إلى العقل

RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r1.claim: With light hamza, “ ألا” is an attention particle followed by a vocative particle whose addressee is omitted; the cited verse illustrates the omission.
RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r1.anchor: للتنبيه ويا حرف النداء ومناداه محذوف

RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r2.claim: With doubled lām, one parsing means Satan turned them from the path lest they prostrate, with a preposition omitted; alternatively “lā” is extra, meaning they are not guided except by prostrating.
RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r2.anchor: فحذف الجار مع أن ويجوز أن تكون لا مزيدة

RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r3.speaker: عبدالله، الأعمش
RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r3.claim: A reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh and al-Aʿmash has “halla,” replacing the hamza with hāʾ.
RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r3.anchor: قراءة الأعمش هلا بقلب الهمزة هاء

RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r4.speaker: عبدالله
RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r4.claim: A further reading from ʿAbd Allāh addresses the audience directly: “Will you not prostrate?”
RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r4.anchor: وعن عبدالله هلا تسجدون بمعنى ألا تسجدون على الخطاب

RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r5.speaker: أبي
RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r5.claim: Abū’s reading has “Do they not prostrate to God?” and continues with God’s bringing forth hidden things and knowing what people conceal and disclose.
RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r5.anchor: قراءة أبي { إلا * يسجدون * لله الذى يخرج الخبء فى * السماوات

RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r6.speaker: أهل التحقيق
RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r6.claim: The investigators say the phrase must be a command: if it prohibited prostration, God’s power to reveal hidden things and knowledge of secrets would not support the wording.
RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r6.anchor: يجب أن يكون بمعنى الأمر لأنه لو كان بمعنى المنع

RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r7.claim: “The hidden thing” is a verbal noun used for what is hidden, encompassing provisions and wealth; God brings it from heaven through rain and from earth through plants.
RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r7.anchor: وهو يتناول جميع أنواع الأرزاق والأموال

RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p164#2/r8.claim: The verse attributes both power to God, who brings hidden things forth, and knowledge, since He knows what people conceal and reveal.

RAZI-FULL:v24p165/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p165/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p165/r1.claim: The argument refutes sun worship: deity requires universal power and knowledge, but the finite sun cannot be shown to bring hidden things forth or know secrets, nor therefore to secure benefits and avert harms.
RAZI-FULL:v24p165/r1.anchor: الشمس ليست كذلك فهي لا تكون إلها

RAZI-FULL:v24p165/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p165/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p165/r2.claim: He also reads heaven’s hidden thing as the sun emerging after its setting, under God’s control; earth’s hidden things include sperm from the loins and ribs and the embryo formed from it.
RAZI-FULL:v24p165/r2.anchor: هو الذي يخرج الشمس من المشرق بعد أفولها في المغرب فهذا هو إخراج الخبء في السموات

RAZI-FULL:v24p165/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p165/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p165/r3.claim: The sun’s setting and rising show it is governed by a sovereign, so worship belongs to its controller; the verse reverses Abraham’s and Moses’ order because this debate concerns sun worship.
RAZI-FULL:v24p165/r3.anchor: أفول الشمس وطلوعها يدلان على كونها تحت تدبير مدبر قاهر فكانت العبادة لقاهرها والمتصرف فيها أولى

STUDYQURAN:27:25/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:25/r1.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:27:25/r1.claim: Both alā and allā are accepted readings; alā links the verse to the previous one, meaning they were turned from the way and did not prostrate.

STUDYQURAN:27:25/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:25/r2.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:27:25/r2.claim: One reported referent of what is hidden is rain.
STUDYQURAN:27:25/r2.anchor: By what is hidden some understand rain

STUDYQURAN:27:25/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:25/r3.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:27:25/r3.claim: Another reported referent is the fruits of the earth.

STUDYQURAN:27:25/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:25/r4.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:27:25/r4.claim: Another reported referent is everything in the heavens and earth known only to God.
STUDYQURAN:27:25/r4.anchor: all things in the heavens and the earth that are known only to God (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:27:25/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:25/r5.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:27:25/r5.claim: Q takes what is hidden to mean mysteries generally.

TAB-FULL:v18p41/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p41/r1.speaker: بعض المكيين وبعض المدنيين والكوفيين
TAB-FULL:v18p41/r1.claim: Some Makkan, Medinan, and Kufan readers lighten ألا and understand an imperative: “Will you not, you there, prostrate?” with the vocative omitted.
TAB-FULL:v18p41/r1.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك أنهما قراءتان مستفيضتان في قراءة الأمصار قد قرأ بكل واحدة منهما علماء من القراء مع صحة معنييهما

TAB-FULL:v18p41/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p41/r2.speaker: قراء المدينة والكوفة والبصرة
TAB-FULL:v18p41/r2.claim: The majority of readers in Medina, Kufa, and Basra double ألا and read it as “so that they not prostrate.”
TAB-FULL:v18p41/r2.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك أنهما قراءتان مستفيضتان في قراءة الأمصار قد قرأ بكل واحدة منهما علماء من القراء مع صحة معنييهما

TAB-FULL:v18p41/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p41/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p41/r3.claim: With the light reading, اسجدوا is jussive and ألا has no syntactic position.
TAB-FULL:v18p41/r3.anchor: فعلى هذه القراءة اسجدوا في هذا الموضع جزم، ولا موضع لقوله «ألا» في الإعراب.

TAB-FULL:v18p41/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p41/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p41/r4.claim: With the doubled reading, ألا occupies an accusative position with the sense لئلا, and يسجدوا is governed by أن.
TAB-FULL:v18p41/r4.anchor: «ألا» في موضع نصب لما ذكرت من معناه أنه لئلا، ويسجدوا في موضع نصب بأن

TAB-FULL:v18p41/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p41/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p41/r5.claim: Both readings are widespread among regional readers and each has a valid meaning.
TAB-FULL:v18p41/r5.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك أنهما قراءتان مستفيضتان في قراءة الأمصار قد قرأ بكل واحدة منهما علماء من القراء مع صحة معنييهما

TAB-FULL:v18p41/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p41/r6.speaker: بعض نحويي البصرة
TAB-FULL:v18p41/r6.claim: A Basran grammarian analyzes the light reading as an imperative with يا inserted for attention, with the meeting of consonants eliding the alifs.
TAB-FULL:v18p41/r6.anchor: فقال بعض نحويي البصرة: من قرأ ذلك كذلك، فكأنه جعله أمرا، كأنه قال لهم: اسجدوا، وزاد «يا» بينهما التي تكون للتنبيه

TAB-FULL:v18p41/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p41/r7.speaker: بعض نحويي الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v18p41/r7.claim: A Kufan grammarian says vocative يا can stand for the omitted addressee, or the addressee can stand in place of يا; this explains the elisions.
TAB-FULL:v18p41/r7.anchor: وقال بعض نحويي الكوفة: هذه «يا» التي تدخل للنداء يكتفى بها من الاسم، ويكتفى بالاسم منها

TAB-FULL:v18p41/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p41/r8.speaker: الأخطل
TAB-FULL:v18p41/r8.claim: The poet’s “ألا يا اسلمي” attests the Arabic vocative construction used to explain the light reading.
TAB-FULL:v18p41/r8.anchor: واستشهد أيضا ببيت الأخطل: [البحر الطويل] ألا يا اسلمي يا هند هند بني بدر

TAB-FULL:v18p43/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p43/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p43/r1.claim: الخبء is what is hidden in heaven or earth, such as rain from heaven and vegetation from earth.
TAB-FULL:v18p43/r1.anchor: قراءة عن مجاهد: " {يخرج الخبء في السموات} قال: الغيث "

TAB-FULL:v18p43/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p43/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p43/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses the hidden thing in the heavens as rain.
TAB-FULL:v18p43/r2.anchor: قراءة عن مجاهد: " {يخرج الخبء في السموات} قال: الغيث "

TAB-FULL:v18p43/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p43/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v18p43/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd describes God’s provision as rain from heaven and plants from earth, after opening the joined sky and earth so rain and growth could emerge.
TAB-FULL:v18p43/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {الذي يخرج الخبء في السموات والأرض} قال: خبء السماء والأرض: ما جعل الله فيها من الأرزاق، والمطر من السماء، والنبات من الأرض

TAB-FULL:v18p43/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p43/r4.speaker: حكيم بن جابر
TAB-FULL:v18p43/r4.claim: Hakim ibn Jabir glosses the phrase as God knowing every hidden thing in the heavens and earth.
TAB-FULL:v18p43/r4.anchor: عن حكيم بن جابر، في قوله: « {ألا يسجدوا لله الذي يخرج الخبء في السموات والأرض} ويعلم كل خفية في السماوات والأرض»

TAB-FULL:v18p43/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p43/r5.speaker: كعب
TAB-FULL:v18p43/r5.claim: Kaʿb says seed comes down from heaven and emerges from earth; Ibn Abbas, who asked about the report, affirmed it.
TAB-FULL:v18p43/r5.anchor: سمعت كعبا يقول: " البذر ينزل من السماء ويخرج من الأرض، قال: صدقت

TAB-FULL:v18p43/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p43/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p43/r6.claim: The phrase uses في for من, as Arabs interchange the prepositions when describing extraction.
TAB-FULL:v18p43/r6.anchor: عن حكيم بن جابر، في قوله: « {ألا يسجدوا لله الذي يخرج الخبء في السموات والأرض} ويعلم كل خفية في السماوات والأرض»

TAB-FULL:v18p44/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p44/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p44/r1.claim: On the doubled ألا reading, God knows the hidden and public affairs of the creatures whose deeds Satan has adorned.
TAB-FULL:v18p44/r1.anchor: وقد ذكر أن ذلك في قراءة أبي: (ألا تسجدوا لله الذي يعلم سركم وما تعلنون)

TAB-FULL:v18p44/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p44/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p44/r2.claim: On the light ألا reading, God knows what the people commanded to prostrate keep secret as well as what they disclose.
TAB-FULL:v18p44/r2.anchor: وقد ذكر أن ذلك في قراءة أبي: (ألا تسجدوا لله الذي يعلم سركم وما تعلنون)

TAB-FULL:v18p44/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p44/r3.speaker: أبي
TAB-FULL:v18p44/r3.claim: Ubayy’s reading says “Will you not prostrate to God, who knows your secret and what you disclose?”
TAB-FULL:v18p44/r3.anchor: وقد ذكر أن ذلك في قراءة أبي: (ألا تسجدوا لله الذي يعلم سركم وما تعلنون)

TABATABAI:27:23-25/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:23-25/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:23-25/r6.claim: The common reading has a doubled lām, combining an and lā; it is an appositional explanation of their deeds: Satan made them not prostrate to God.
TABATABAI:27:23-25/r6.anchor: القراءة الدائرة { ألا } - بتشديد اللام - مؤلف من

TABATABAI:27:23-25/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:23-25/r7.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:27:23-25/r7.claim: A second analysis supplies a purpose lām: Satan beautified their misguidance so they would not prostrate to God.
TABATABAI:27:23-25/r7.anchor: وقيل بتقدير لام التعليل، والمعنى زين لهم الشيطان ضلالتهم لئلا يسجدوا لله

TABATABAI:27:23-25/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:23-25/r8.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:27:23-25/r8.claim: Majmaʿ al-Bayān defines khabʾ as something concealed by a covering that prevents perception; it is a verbal noun used adjectivally, and what God brings from nonexistence has that status.
TABATABAI:27:23-25/r8.anchor: والخبء على ما في مجمع البيان المخبوء وهو ما أحاط به غيره حتى منع من إدراكه

TABATABAI:27:23-25/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:23-25/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:23-25/r9.claim: The author reads bringing forth hidden things as a metaphor for creating them from nonexistence, like splitting nonexistence when God is called the Originator of the heavens and earth.
TABATABAI:27:23-25/r9.anchor: ففي قوله { يخرج الخبء في السماوات والأرض } استعارة كأن الأشياء مخبوءة مستورة تحت أطباق العدم

TABATABAI:27:23-25/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:23-25/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:23-25/r10.claim: The author allows a literal reading of bringing out the hidden but says it needs an explanation of where it is hidden, supplied elsewhere.
TABATABAI:27:23-25/r10.anchor: ويمكن حمل الجملة على الحقيقة من غير استعارة لكنه مفتقر إلى بيان موضعه غير هذا الموضع

TABATABAI:27:23-25/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:23-25/r11.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:27:23-25/r11.claim: A reported view defines the hidden as the unseen and bringing it forth as knowing it; the author dismisses this interpretation.
TABATABAI:27:23-25/r11.anchor: وقيل المراد بالخبء الغيب وإخراجه العلم به وهو كما ترى

TABATABAI:27:23-25/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:23-25/r12.speaker: الأكثرون
TABATABAI:27:23-25/r12.claim: The phrase is read by some with second-person tāʾ, “what you conceal and disclose,” and by the majority with third-person yāʾ; the author favors the majority reading.
TABATABAI:27:23-25/r12.anchor: وقوله { ويعلم ما تخفون وما تعلنون } بالتاء على الخطاب أي يعلم سركم وعلانيتكم، وقرأ الأكثرون بالياء على الغيبة وهو أرجح

TABATABAI:27:23-25/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:23-25/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:23-25/r13.claim: Since God brings all things from nonexistence, including the sun and its governance, He alone deserves worship; the sun is unaware of worshippers, while God knows what is hidden and open.
TABATABAI:27:23-25/r13.anchor: فالله سبحانه هو المتعين للسجدة والتعظيم لا غير

TABRISI:27:20-26/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:20-26/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:20-26/r1.claim: The light reading of allā yāsjudū is construed as an address with an omitted vocative such as qawm; the supplied poetry illustrates this deletion.
TABRISI:27:20-26/r1.anchor: وكذلك ما حكي عن أبي عمرو من قوله يا ويل له ويجوز أن يراد بعد يا مأمورون فحذفوا

TABRISI:27:20-26/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:20-26/r2.speaker: أبو زيد
TABRISI:27:20-26/r2.claim: Abu Zayd's verse about being told ya-smaʿ illustrates an omitted person addressed after yā.
TABRISI:27:20-26/r2.anchor: فمن تلك ما أنشده أبو زيد:

TABRISI:27:20-26/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:20-26/r3.speaker: ذو الرمة
TABRISI:27:20-26/r3.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's greeting to the dwelling of May provides another poetic example of the vocative construction.

TABRISI:27:20-26/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:20-26/r4.speaker: الأخطل
TABRISI:27:20-26/r4.claim: Al-Akhtal's greeting to Hind is cited as a further poetic example of the same vocative pattern.
TABRISI:27:20-26/r4.anchor: وللأخطل: ألا يا اسلمي يا هند

TABRISI:27:20-26/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:20-26/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:20-26/r5.claim: The mushaf's written yāʾ supports the geminated reading allā yasjudū; the light reading would instead have the imperative asjudū without yāʾ.
TABRISI:27:20-26/r5.anchor: ومما يؤكد قراءة من قرأ ألا يسجدوا بالتشديد أنها لو كانت مخففة لما كانت في يسجدوا ياء لأنها اسجدوا

TABRISI:27:20-26/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:20-26/r6.speaker: الكسائي
TABRISI:27:20-26/r6.claim: Readers use third-person yukhfūn/yʿlinūn because the discourse is in third person; al-Kisaʾi uses second-person forms as the discourse shifts to address on asjudū.
TABRISI:27:20-26/r6.anchor: ومن قرأ يخفون ويعلنون بالياء فلأن الكلام على الغيبة وقراءة الكسائي فيهما بالتاء لأن الكلام قد دخله خطاب

TABRISI:27:20-26/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:20-26/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:20-26/r7.claim: The variant allā yā asjudū can address both believers and disbelievers previously mentioned in the third person.
TABRISI:27:20-26/r7.anchor: ومن قرأ ألا يا اسجدوا فيجوز أن يكون الخطاب للمؤمنين والكافرين الذين جرى ذكرهم على لفظ الغيبة

TABRISI:27:24-25/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:24-25/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:24-25/r10.claim: Tabrisi rejects al-Jubbāʾī: distinguishing worship of God from sun worship as right and wrong requires knowledge of God, and attributing misguidance to Satan implies knowledge of divine justice.
TABRISI:27:24-25/r10.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكره خلاف ظاهر القرآن لأنه لا يجوز أن يفرق بين الحق الذي هو السجود لله

TABRISI:27:24-25/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:24-25/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:24-25/r11.claim: With lightening, allā yāsjudū can command prostration, with a warning yāʾ or an omitted qawm; it may also be a divine command interjected into the account or the hoopoe's protest to Sabaʾ or Sulayman.
TABRISI:27:24-25/r11.anchor: قد بينا أن التخفيف إنما هو على معنى الأمر بالسجود ودخلت الياء للتنبيه

TABRISI:27:24-25/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:24-25/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:24-25/r12.claim: The geminated reading means Satan made their misguidance attractive so that they would not prostrate to God.
TABRISI:27:24-25/r12.anchor: والقراءة بالتشديد على معنى زين لهم الشيطان ضلالتهم لئلا يسجدوا لله

TABRISI:27:24-25/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:24-25/r13.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:27:24-25/r13.claim: Al-Farra says the geminated reading does not require a prostration of recitation.
TABRISI:27:24-25/r13.anchor: وذكر الفراء إن القراءة بالتشديد لا توجب سجدة التلاوة

TABRISI:27:24-25/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:24-25/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:24-25/r14.claim: Tabrisi rejects al-Farra: the wording reproaches them for leaving prostration and therefore indicates that prostration is obligatory, as in 25:60.
TABRISI:27:24-25/r14.anchor: وهذا غير صحيح لأن الكلام قد تضمن الذم على ترك السجود فيه دلالة على وجوب السجود

TABRISI:27:25-26/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:25-26/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:25-26/r1.claim: Khabʾ is something hidden behind a barrier that prevents detection; the verbal noun is used adjectivally, and what God creates from nothing is like a hidden thing brought out.
TABRISI:27:25-26/r1.anchor: الخبء المخبوء وهو ما أحاط به غيره حتى منع من إدراكه وهو مصدر وصف به

TABRISI:27:25-26/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:25-26/r2.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد
TABRISI:27:25-26/r2.claim: Ikrima and Mujahid take khabʾ as the unseen: everything hidden from perception in the heavens and earth.
TABRISI:27:25-26/r2.anchor: وقيل: الخبء الغيب وهو كل ما غاب عن الإدراك فالمعنى يعلم غيب السماوات والأرض عن عكرمة ومجاهد

TABRISI:27:25-26/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:25-26/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TABRISI:27:25-26/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies heaven's hidden thing as rain and earth's as plants and trees.
TABRISI:27:25-26/r3.anchor: وقيل: أن خبء السماوات المطر وخبء الأرض النبات والأشجار عن ابن زيد

TABRISI:27:25-26/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:25-26/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:25-26/r4.claim: What people conceal and reveal means what is secret and public.

TABRISI:27:25-26/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:25-26/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:25-26/r5.claim: The statement through Lord of the great throne may finish the hoopoe's speech or begin God's own report.
TABRISI:27:25-26/r5.anchor: إلى ههنا تمام الحكاية لما قاله الهدهد ويحتمل أن يكون ابتداء إخبار من الله تعالى

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p323#7/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p323#7/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p323#7/r1.claim: Al-khabʾ is what is concealed in the heavens or earth, from khabaʾtu al-shayʾ, “I hid the thing.”
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p323#7/r1.anchor: الذي يخرج الخبء في السماوات والأرض} أي المستتر فيهما.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p323#7/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p323#7/r2.speaker: غير مسمى
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p323#7/r2.claim: A common saying calls rain the hidden thing of heaven and vegetation the hidden thing of earth.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p323#7/r2.anchor: خبء السماء: المطر. وخبء الأرض: النبات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r1.claim: With the doubled reading, the construction means Satan turned them from the path so that they would not prostrate; the omitted lām marks purpose, and أن is accusative after faṣaddahum.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r1.anchor: فمن شدد فتقديرها: فصدهم عن السبيل لئلا يسجدوا. وهذا قول الزجاج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r2.claim: An may instead depend on zayyana: Satan made their deeds seem good so that they would not prostrate; the lām is omitted and أن may be accusative or genitive.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يعلق: أن، بزين؛ كأنه زين لهم الشيطان لئلا يسجدوا. وهذا قول الفراء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r3.claim: The doubled reading best preserves the story's flow without an interruption, though an intervening parenthesis is possible and could reinforce the narrative.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r3.anchor: والوجه: قراءة من قرأ بالتشديد لتجري القصة على سننها، ولا يفصل بين بعضها وبعض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r4.claim: The hoopoe's address is effectively O people or O Muslims, prostrate to God, opposing the others and praising God for guiding them to monotheism.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r4.anchor: قال الهدهد: ألا يا قوم، أو يا مسلمون اسجدوا لله الذي خلق السموات والأرض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r5.claim: The alerting particle before the command appeals to the audience and strengthens the order, like a vocative that draws a listener toward what follows.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r5.anchor: ووجه دخول حرف التنبيه على الأمر، أنه: موضع يحتاج فيه إلى استعطاف المأمور

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r6.claim: There may be no actual vocative after ألا, or a vocative such as O commanded ones may be understood and omitted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r6.anchor: فقد يجوز أن لا يريد منادى في نحو قوله: {ألا يسجدوا} ويجوز أن يراد بعد يا: مأمورون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r7.claim: A cited line beginning O curse of God must address an omitted audience, such as O people or O these, not the curse itself.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r7.anchor: يا لعنة الله والأقوام كلهم ... والصالحين على سمعان من جار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r8.speaker: أبو زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r8.claim: A poetic example likewise uses O with an omitted addressee before the command to listen.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r8.anchor: من ذلك ما أنشده أبو زيد: وقالت ألا يا اسمع نعظك بخطة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r9.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r9.claim: With the light reading, the sense is O these, prostrate; hāʾulāʾ is understood and represented by yāʾ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p208#2/r9.anchor: قال الفراء: من قرأ بالتخفيف فهو على معنى: ألا يا هؤلاء اسجدوا، فيضمر: هؤلاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p214/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p214/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p214/r1.claim: Khabʾ is something hidden away or stored for a future need; anything one hides is a khabʾ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p214/r1.anchor: يقال: خبأت الشيء أخبؤه، خبأ. والخبء: ما خبأت من ذخيرة ليوم ما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p214/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p214/r2.speaker: مجاهد ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p214/r2.claim: They identify the hidden thing in the heavens and earth as rain.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p214/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد ومقاتل: يعني: الغيث في السماوات والأرض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p214/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p214/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p214/r3.claim: A transmitted interpretation takes it as rain from heaven and plants from earth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p214/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج: وجاء في التفسير أن الخبء هاهنا: القطر من السماء، والنبات من الأرض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p214/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p214/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p214/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the best sense is everything hidden, meaning the unseen in heaven and earth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p214/r4.anchor: قال: ويجوز وهو الوجه أن الخبء: كل ما غاب، فيكون المعنى: يعلم الغيب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p214/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p214/r5.speaker: عبد الله
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p214/r5.claim: A reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh has the hidden thing brought forth in the heavens.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p214/r5.anchor: وذكر الفراء القولين أيضا، وقال: وهي في قراءة عبد الله: {يخرج الخبء في السماوات}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p214/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p214/r6.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p214/r6.claim: Fī can stand where min is intended, as in extracting knowledge that is in someone from that person; one preposition can be omitted while the sense remains.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p214/r6.anchor: قال: وصلحت: (في) مكان: (من)؛ لأنك تقول: لأستخرجن العلم فيكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p215/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p215/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p215/r1.claim: Most readers use the third-person yāʾ, matching the surrounding third-person narration.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p215/r1.anchor: قراءة الناس بالياء؛ لأن الكلام على الغيبة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p215/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p215/r2.speaker: الكسائي وحفص
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p215/r2.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and Ḥafṣ use second-person tāʾ; al-Kisāʾī's reading follows his light reading of ألا يسجدوا, which introduces direct address.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p215/r2.anchor: أما الكسائي فإن الكلام دخله خطاب على قراءته: {ألا يسجدوا} بالتخفيف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p215/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p215/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p215/r3.claim: On the second-person reading, the command means: prostrate to God, who knows what you conceal.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p215/r3.anchor: والمعنى: اسجدوا لله الذي يعلم ما تخفون.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p215/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p215/r4.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p215/r4.claim: Abū Bakr's report from ʿĀṣim with yāʾ fits his recitation better than Ḥafṣ's report, since both clauses remain third person.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p215/r4.anchor: ورواية أبي بكر عن عاصم بالياء أشبه بقراءته من رواية حفص؛ لأنه غيبة مع غيبة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p215/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p215/r5.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p215/r5.claim: What they conceal is in their hearts, and what they reveal is with their tongues.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p215/r5.anchor: قال مقاتل: {ما تخفون} في قلوبهم {وما تعلنون} بألسنتهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:25/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:25/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:25/r1.claim: The phrase is explained as “so that they do not prostrate to God.”
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:25/r1.anchor: ألا يسجدوا } أي: لأن لا يسجدوا لله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:25/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:25/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:25/r2.claim: What God brings forth from concealment is rain from the sky and vegetation from the earth.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:25/r2.anchor: القطر من السماء، والنبات من الأرض

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p539/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p539/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p539/r4.claim: Yahya says the clause order is advanced: Satan adorned their deeds and barred them from the way, keeping them from prostrating to God and guidance.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p539/r4.anchor: وفيها تقديم، أي: وزين لهم الشيطان أعمالهم فصدهم عن السبيل ألا يسجدوا لله، فصدهم عن الطريق بتركهم السجود

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p539/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p539/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p539/r5.claim: Yahya cites an Arabic usage in which “a-lā tasjudū” can function as “indeed, prostrate.”
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p539/r5.anchor: وفي بعض كلام العرب: ألا تسجدوا ألا فاسجدوا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p540/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p540/r1.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p540/r1.claim: Qatadah glosses the hidden thing in heaven and earth as the secret; the word derives from something concealed.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p540/r1.anchor: قال قتادة: أي: يعلم السر في السماوات والأرض، والخبء من الخبيئة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p540/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p540/r3.speaker: يحيى
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p540/r3.claim: Yahya notes that the word is singular.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p540/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p540/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p540/r4.claim: God knows what people conceal in their breasts.

MAJAZ:v2p94/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p94/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p94/r1.claim: Al-khabʾ is what one has concealed within oneself, or kept secret.
MAJAZ:v2p94/r1.anchor: الذي يخرج الخبء في السماوات والأرض» (25) ما خبأت فى نفسك أي ما أسررت..

BURHAN:v3p179/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p179/r1.speaker: أبو علي
BURHAN:v3p179/r1.claim: Abū ʿAlī says the disagreement over an omitted circumstantial element is about analogy: Sībawayh restricts it to attested usage, while al-Akhfash and al-Mubarrad analogize it.
BURHAN:v3p179/r1.anchor: قال أبو علي لا خلاف بين سيبويه وأبي العباس في الحال المحذوف الذي المصدر منصوب به وإنما الخلاف بينهما في القياس

BURHAN:v3p179/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p179/r2.speaker: الكسائي
BURHAN:v3p179/r2.claim: On al-Kisāʾī’s lightened reading, the phrase is an alert plus a vocative—“O these, prostrate”—or two alerts without a vocative, combined to draw the commanded person’s attention.
BURHAN:v3p179/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ ألا يسجدوا ﴾ 1 على قراءة الكسائي بتخفيف ألا على أنها تنبيه ويا نداء

BURHAN:v3p179/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p179/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p179/r3.claim: On the majority’s strengthened reading, أن governs the imperfect and لا negates it; the verb is inflected and loses its nūn as the sign of the subjunctive.
BURHAN:v3p179/r3.anchor: وأما على قراءة الأكثر بالتشديد فعلى أن أن الناصبة للفعل دخلت عليها لا النافية والفعل المضارع بعدها منصوب وحذفت النون علامة النصب

BURHAN:v4p445/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p445/r2.speaker: ابن فارس
BURHAN:v4p445/r2.claim: Ibn Fāris says the particle alā may express regret and grief, as in “will they not prostrate”; another view takes it as an alert particle.
BURHAN:v4p445/r2.anchor: قال ابن فارس تأنى للتأسف والتلهف نحو ﴿ ألا يسجدوا ﴾ 5 وقيل للتنبيه

BURHAN:v4p445/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p445/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p445/r3.claim: Alā can also express delight, as in the cited line wishing that the beloved’s coolness on the heart would stay.
BURHAN:v4p445/r3.anchor: وللتلذذ نحو … يا بردها على الفؤاد لو تقف

ITQAN:v2p442/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p442/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p442/r1.claim: The author says ألا with a fatḥa and shadda is an exhortative particle and suggests this may be its only Quranic use, in ألا يسجدوا لله.
ITQAN:v2p442/r1.anchor: بالفتح والتشديد حرف تحضيض ولم يقع في القرآن لهذا المعنى فيما أعلم

NAHHAS:v3p206/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p206/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو وعاصم ونافع وحمزة
NAHHAS:v3p206/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, Nāfiʿ, and Ḥamza read ألا يسجدوا; its أن is accusative when construed as an inserted particle.
NAHHAS:v3p206/r1.anchor: هذه قراءة أبي عمرو وعاصم ونافع وحمزة وقرأ الزهري وأبو جعفر وأبو عبد الرحمن

NAHHAS:v3p206/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p206/r2.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v3p206/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash interprets the reading as “so that they do not prostrate.”
NAHHAS:v3p206/r2.anchor: قال الأخفش المعنى لئلا يسجدوا وقال الكسائي المعنى فصدهم أن لا يسجدوا

NAHHAS:v3p206/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p206/r3.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v3p206/r3.claim: Al-Kisāʾī understands that Satan turned them away from prostrating to God.
NAHHAS:v3p206/r3.anchor: وقال الكسائي المعنى فصدهم أن لا يسجدوا وقال علي بن سليمان أن بدل من أعمالهم

NAHHAS:v3p206/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p206/r4.speaker: علي بن سليمان
NAHHAS:v3p206/r4.claim: ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān takes أن as an accusative appositive to أعمالهم; another analysis makes it a genitive appositive to السبيل.
NAHHAS:v3p206/r4.anchor: وقال علي بن سليمان أن بدل من أعمالهم في موضع نصب وقيل موضعها خفض على البدل من السبيل

NAHHAS:v3p206/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p206/r5.speaker: الزهري وأبو جعفر وأبو عبد الرحمن وحميد وطلحة والكسائي
NAHHAS:v3p206/r5.claim: Al-Zuhrī, Abū Jaʿfar, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Ḥumayd, Ṭalḥa, and al-Kisāʾī read ألا يا اسجدوا, addressing “these people.”
NAHHAS:v3p206/r5.anchor: وقرأ الزهري وأبو جعفر وأبو عبد الرحمن وحميد وطلحة والكسائي ( ألا يا اسجدوا لله )

NAHHAS:v3p206/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p206/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p206/r6.claim: The second reading means “O people, prostrate”; two poetic examples support vocative yā, though al-Naḥḥās calls the construction unusual and the reading remote because it interrupts the syntax and differs from the written consonantal text.
NAHHAS:v3p206/r6.anchor: القراءة الثانية بمعنى ألا يا هؤلاء اسجدوا

NAHHAS:v3p206/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p206/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p206/r7.claim: At pause the hamza is still; in nominative it may have ḍamma or imālah, but it cannot be geminated.
NAHHAS:v3p206/r7.anchor: والوقف عليه بتسكين الهمزة وإذا كان في موضع رفع جاز الضم والأشمام ولا يجوز التضعيف

NAHHAS:v3p206/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p206/r8.speaker: عكرمة
NAHHAS:v3p206/r8.claim: ʿIkrima is reported to read الخبا with an alif and no hamza; Abū Ḥātim says this is not valid Arabic, arguing that easing hamza would produce الخب or الخبي.
NAHHAS:v3p206/r8.anchor: وحكى أبو حاتم أن عكرمة قرأ ( الذي يخرج الخبا في السموات والأرض ) بألف غير مهموزة

NAHHAS:v3p206/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p206/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p206/r9.claim: Al-Naḥḥās rejects Abū Ḥātim’s claim: Sībawayh records hamza changing to alif, wāw, or yāʾ after a still consonant according to its vowel, including in الخبء.
NAHHAS:v3p206/r9.anchor: قال أبو جعفر قوله لا يجوز الخبا وسمعت علي بن سليمان يقول سمعت محمد بن يزيد يقول كان دون أصحابه في النحو ولم يلحق بهم يعني أبا حاتم

NAHHAS:v3p206/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p206/r10.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v3p206/r10.claim: Sībawayh records dialects replacing hamza with a matching long vowel after sukūn and examples such as هذا الخبو, عجبت من الخبي, and رأيت الخبا; some Tamīm and Asad speakers instead retain hamza and alter the preceding vowel.
NAHHAS:v3p206/r10.anchor: حكى سيبويه عن العرب أنها تبدل من الهمزة ألفا إذا كان قبلها ساكن وكانت مفتوحة وتبدل منها واوا إذا كان قبلها ساكن وكانت مضمومة

NAHHAS:v3p206/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p206/r11.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v3p206/r11.claim: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd is quoted as judging Abū Ḥātim less accomplished in grammar than his peers, though outside his home region he met no one more learned.
NAHHAS:v3p206/r11.anchor: سمعت علي بن سليمان يقول سمعت محمد بن يزيد يقول كان دون أصحابه في النحو ولم يلحق بهم يعني أبا حاتم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f9.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f9.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f9.claim: Sībawayh reports a softened reading of ألا يسجدوا, transmitted by ʿĪsā, and explains it as hamza deletion when the reciter avoids full articulation.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f9.anchor: حدثنا بذلك عيسى وإنما حذفت الهمزة ههنا لأنك

BURHAN:v1p44/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p44/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p44/r2.claim: The passage about the Queen of Sheba's sun-worship turns toward the call to prostrate to God, illustrating a transition in the discourse.
BURHAN:v1p44/r2.anchor: فهم لا يهتدون ألا يسجدوا لله

BURHAN:v2p140/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p140/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p140/r3.claim: The general wording about bringing hidden things forth confirms the report: the Quran focuses on the dead emerging alive, while the hadith focuses on treasures and minerals.
BURHAN:v2p140/r3.anchor: فتوجه القرآن إلى الإخبار عن إخراجها الأموات أحياء وتوجه الحديث إلى الإخبار عن إخراجها كنوزها ومعادنها

BURHAN:v4p235/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p235/r4.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v4p235/r4.claim: The source records opposing analyses of which form is primary: the stressed form or the light form.
BURHAN:v4p235/r4.anchor: ثم قيل المشددة اصل والمخففة فرع قيل بالعكس

ITQAN:v3p222#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p222#2/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p222#2/r6.claim: Other figurative vocative functions include singling someone out, alerting, expressing astonishment, and expressing regret.
ITQAN:v3p222#2/r6.anchor: التنبيه كقوله ﴿ ألا يسجدوا ﴾ والتعجب كقوله ﴿ يا حسرة على العباد ﴾

ITQAN:v2p325/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p325/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p325/r3.claim: The hidden thing (al-khabʾ) is whatever is concealed in heaven and earth; the phrase means “He knows every hidden thing.”
ITQAN:v2p325/r3.anchor: 1876 ﴿ يخرج الخبء ﴾ يعلم كل خفية في السماء والأرض

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p348/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p348/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p348/r2.claim: Sujūd can mean ritual prostration, placing the forehead on the ground.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p348/r2.anchor: أحدها : السجود الشرعي ، وهو وضع الجبهة على الأرض

NASHR:v2p337/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p337/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر والكسائي ورويس
NASHR:v2p337/r5.claim: They lighten the lām, pause after ألا يا, then begin اسجدوا as an imperative; the vocative addresses people, and the written hamzat al-waṣl is omitted for connected reading.
NASHR:v2p337/r5.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر والكسائي، ورويس بتخفيف اللام

NASHR:v2p337/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p337/r7.speaker: الكسائي وحفص
NASHR:v2p337/r7.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and Ḥafṣ address the hearers directly in both verbs; the rest read third-person forms.
NASHR:v2p337/r7.anchor: فقرأ الكسائي وحفص بالخطاب فيهما، وقرأهما الباقون بالغيب
